records.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
records.methodology_paraphrase:
An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale

The image is divided into fixed-size patches, and each patch is flattened and linearly projected into a token embedding. A learnable class token and positional embeddings are appended to the sequence, which is then processed by a standard Transformer encoder composed of multi-head self-attention and MLP blocks with residual connections and layer normalization. The final class-token representation is used for classification. The paper emphasizes large-scale pre-training followed by fine-tuning, showing that a pure patch-based Transformer can replace convolutional feature extractors when sufficient data are available.

records.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition

The network is organized as a stack of residual blocks that learn a residual function with respect to the block input rather than a complete transformation from scratch. Each block computes a sequence of convolution, normalization, and nonlinear operations and adds the original input through an identity shortcut; projection shortcuts are used when spatial dimensions or channel counts change. This formulation allows very deep networks to propagate information and gradients more effectively. The paper evaluates bottleneck residual blocks for deep ImageNet models and reuses the same residual representation as a backbone for detection and localization.

records.title: Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Visualizing and Understanding Convolutional Networks

The method analyzes intermediate convolutional representations using a deconvolutional visualization procedure that maps feature activations back into pixel space. Insights from these visualizations are used to modify the earlier ImageNet convolutional architecture, including the first-layer filter size and stride, so that low-level information is preserved more effectively. The network remains a conventional deep convolutional classifier with alternating convolution, nonlinearity, pooling, and fully connected stages, but the architecture is refined through direct inspection of learned feature responses and occlusion experiments rather than by increasing depth alone.

records.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition

The architecture studies depth as the main design variable while keeping the convolutional building block deliberately simple. All spatial convolutions use small 3×3 kernels with stride one, and spatial resolution is reduced by 2×2 max pooling. As depth increases, the number of feature channels grows while the receptive field expands through repeated small convolutions. The final representation is passed through fully connected classification layers. By standardizing the local operator and systematically increasing network depth, the method demonstrates that deep stacks of small convolutions provide a strong and transferable visual representation.

records.title: Going Deeper with Convolutions
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Going Deeper with Convolutions

The core Inception module processes the same input through several branches in parallel, including 1×1, 3×3, and 5×5 convolutions together with a pooling branch, and concatenates their outputs along the channel dimension. Computational cost is controlled by inserting 1×1 bottleneck convolutions before expensive spatial convolutions. Multiple Inception modules are stacked to build a deep but parameter-efficient network. Auxiliary classifiers are attached to intermediate layers during training to improve gradient flow and regularization, while global average pooling replaces large fully connected layers near the output.

records.title: Densely Connected Convolutional Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Densely Connected Convolutional Networks

Each layer receives as input the concatenation of feature maps produced by all preceding layers within the same dense block. Rather than repeatedly relearning redundant representations, the network preserves earlier features and lets later layers directly reuse them. A small growth rate controls how many new channels each layer contributes, while transition layers with 1×1 convolution and pooling compress and downsample between dense blocks. This dense connectivity shortens gradient paths, encourages feature reuse, and enables deep networks with comparatively few parameters while retaining strong representational capacity.

records.title: EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
EfficientNet: Rethinking Model Scaling for Convolutional Neural Networks

The method begins with a mobile convolutional baseline discovered by neural architecture search and introduces compound scaling to enlarge the network in a balanced way. A single compound coefficient controls depth, width, and input resolution using fixed scaling exponents selected under a resource constraint. The building block is an inverted residual MBConv with squeeze-and-excitation and swish-like activations. Instead of independently increasing only layers, channels, or image size, EfficientNet jointly scales all three dimensions so that additional computation is distributed across the architecture in a consistent manner.

records.title: MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications

The network factorizes a standard convolution into a depthwise convolution, which applies one spatial filter independently to each input channel, followed by a 1×1 pointwise convolution that mixes information across channels. This factorization reduces multiply-add operations and parameter count while retaining a conventional feed-forward CNN structure. Two global hyperparameters, a width multiplier and a resolution multiplier, allow the same architecture to trade accuracy for latency and memory. The design is explicitly optimized for mobile and embedded inference rather than maximum desktop-scale accuracy.

records.title: MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks

MobileNetV2 introduces an inverted residual block in which a low-dimensional input is first expanded with a 1×1 convolution, processed by a depthwise spatial convolution, and projected back to a narrow output using a linear 1×1 layer. Residual shortcuts connect the narrow bottlenecks when the shapes match. The final projection deliberately omits a nonlinear activation so that information is not destroyed in low-dimensional spaces. This combination of depthwise separable convolution, expansion, linear bottlenecks, and thin shortcut-connected representations yields an efficient mobile feature extractor.

records.title: Searching for MobileNetV3
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Searching for MobileNetV3

The architecture combines platform-aware neural architecture search with manual network refinement. Candidate blocks use MobileNetV2-style inverted residual bottlenecks, squeeze-and-excitation, and hardware-friendly nonlinearities such as hard-swish. The search optimizes layer configuration under mobile latency constraints, while later layers are redesigned to reduce expensive operations without sacrificing representation quality. Separate Large and Small configurations target different resource budgets. The methodology therefore treats efficiency as a joint architecture-and-hardware optimization problem rather than simply compressing a conventional CNN after training.

records.title: ShuffleNet: An Extremely Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Mobile Devices
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ShuffleNet: An Extremely Efficient Convolutional Neural Network for Mobile Devices

The network reduces the cost of pointwise convolutions by replacing dense 1×1 operations with grouped pointwise convolution. Because isolated channel groups would restrict information exchange, the output channels are reshaped and permuted by a channel-shuffle operation before subsequent grouped convolutions. Each unit also contains an efficient depthwise convolution for spatial processing and uses residual or concatenation shortcuts depending on stride. The resulting block maintains cross-channel communication while dramatically lowering computation, making the architecture suitable for very small FLOP budgets.

records.title: ShuffleNet V2: Practical Guidelines for Efficient CNN Architecture Design
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ShuffleNet V2: Practical Guidelines for Efficient CNN Architecture Design

Rather than optimizing only theoretical FLOPs, the method derives practical efficiency rules from memory access cost, degree of parallelism, and element-wise operations. The proposed unit splits the input channels into two branches: one branch is kept mostly unchanged, while the other applies pointwise, depthwise, and pointwise convolutions. The branches are concatenated and channel-shuffled, avoiding expensive grouped pointwise convolutions used in the first ShuffleNet. This design reduces fragmentation and memory overhead while maintaining feature exchange across channels and high throughput on real hardware.

records.title: SqueezeNet: AlexNet-level Accuracy with 50x Fewer Parameters and <0.5MB Model Size
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SqueezeNet: AlexNet-level Accuracy with 50x Fewer Parameters and <0.5MB Model Size

The network is built from Fire modules. Each Fire module first uses a squeeze layer of 1×1 convolutions to reduce the number of input channels, then expands the representation through a mixture of 1×1 and 3×3 convolutions. By aggressively limiting the number of channels entering 3×3 filters and delaying spatial downsampling, the architecture preserves activation resolution while greatly reducing parameter count. The classifier uses convolution and global average pooling rather than large fully connected layers, producing a compact model intended for low-memory deployment.

records.title: A ConvNet for the 2020s
records.methodology_paraphrase:
A ConvNet for the 2020s

ConvNeXt starts from a ResNet-style convolutional backbone and progressively incorporates design choices that became common in modern vision Transformers while retaining convolution as the core spatial operator. The network adopts a patchify-like stem, larger depthwise convolution kernels, inverted bottleneck channel expansion, fewer activation and normalization layers, and LayerNorm in place of BatchNorm in key locations. Stage ratios and training recipes are modernized as well. The result is a hierarchical pure ConvNet that preserves the inductive bias and deployment simplicity of convolution while matching contemporary Transformer backbones.

records.title: Aggregated Residual Transformations for Deep Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Aggregated Residual Transformations for Deep Neural Networks

ResNeXt retains the residual learning framework but replaces a single transformation inside each block with a set of parallel transformations having the same topology. These branches are implemented efficiently with grouped convolution, and their outputs are aggregated before the residual addition. The architecture introduces cardinality—the number of parallel transformation groups—as a new capacity dimension alongside depth and width. Increasing cardinality improves representational power without requiring complicated heterogeneous branches, giving a simple repeated block that scales effectively for image recognition.

records.title: Wide Residual Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Wide Residual Networks

The method questions whether extreme depth is always the best way to increase residual-network capacity. It constructs residual networks with substantially wider convolutional layers but fewer total blocks, using a widening factor to multiply the number of channels in each stage. Standard residual shortcuts are retained, and dropout can be inserted inside residual blocks for additional regularization. This wider design improves parallel computation and can optimize more easily than very deep thin networks, demonstrating that channel capacity is an effective alternative to simply stacking more residual layers.

records.title: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks

A squeeze-and-excitation block is inserted into a conventional convolutional unit to adaptively recalibrate channel responses. Global average pooling first compresses each feature map into a channel descriptor. A small two-layer gating network then learns nonlinear inter-channel dependencies and produces a per-channel scale vector. The original feature maps are multiplied by these learned weights before they are passed forward or added through a residual path. The module is lightweight, architecture-agnostic, and can be attached to ResNet, Inception, and other CNN backbones to provide dynamic channel attention.

records.title: Selective Kernel Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Selective Kernel Networks

Selective Kernel units create multiple convolutional branches with different effective receptive fields and let the network choose among them dynamically for each input. Branch features are first aggregated into a global descriptor, which is passed through a compact gating network to produce attention weights over kernel branches. A softmax competition generates channel-wise selection coefficients, and the weighted branches are fused into the output feature. The mechanism allows receptive field size to adapt to image content rather than being fixed by architecture design.

records.title: CBAM: Convolutional Block Attention Module
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CBAM: Convolutional Block Attention Module

CBAM augments a convolutional feature map with two lightweight attention stages applied sequentially. Channel attention aggregates spatial information using global average and max pooling, feeds the descriptors through a shared MLP, and produces channel-wise gates. Spatial attention then compresses the channel dimension using average and max statistics, concatenates the resulting maps, and applies a convolution to produce a spatial gate. Multiplying both gates with the incoming feature map allows the network to emphasize informative channels and spatial locations with little additional computation.

records.title: ECA-Net: Efficient Channel Attention for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ECA-Net: Efficient Channel Attention for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks

The method removes the dimensionality-reduction bottleneck used in many channel-attention modules. Global average pooling first produces a channel descriptor, and a fast one-dimensional convolution is applied directly across neighboring channel values to capture local cross-channel interaction. The kernel size of this 1D convolution is adaptively chosen as a function of the channel dimension. A sigmoid then generates channel weights that rescale the original feature map. This design provides channel attention with very few parameters while preserving direct correspondence between channels and attention weights.

records.title: Designing Network Design Spaces
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Designing Network Design Spaces

Rather than searching individual architectures, the work defines a low-dimensional design space for families of convolutional networks. Network widths are generated from a simple quantized linear rule across depth, and stages are formed by grouping blocks with the same width. The authors progressively simplify and constrain the space using empirical distributions of strong models, resulting in RegNet families whose depth, initial width, slope, group width, and bottleneck ratio are governed by interpretable parameters. Models can then be sampled or optimized within this regularized space for different compute budgets.

records.title: CSPNet: A New Backbone that can Enhance Learning Capability of CNN
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CSPNet: A New Backbone that can Enhance Learning Capability of CNN

Cross Stage Partial connections split the feature map of a stage into two parts. One part is processed through a conventional stack of residual or dense blocks, while the other bypasses the stack and is merged later at the stage transition. This partition reduces duplicated gradient information and decreases computation and memory traffic while preserving feature diversity. The method can be applied to backbones such as ResNet, ResNeXt, and DenseNet, producing CSP variants that improve efficiency in recognition and detection pipelines.

records.title: Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Visual Recognition
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Deep High-Resolution Representation Learning for Visual Recognition

HRNet maintains a high-resolution feature stream throughout the network instead of recovering spatial detail only after aggressive downsampling. Additional lower-resolution branches are introduced gradually, and repeated multi-scale fusion modules exchange information across all resolutions using upsampling or strided transformations. Each resolution is therefore updated using representations from the others while the original high-resolution stream remains active. This parallel multi-resolution design produces spatially precise and semantically strong features, which are especially useful for pose estimation, segmentation, and dense prediction.

records.title: GhostNet: More Features from Cheap Operations
records.methodology_paraphrase:
GhostNet: More Features from Cheap Operations

The architecture observes that many convolutional feature maps are redundant and can be approximated from a smaller set of intrinsic features. A Ghost module first computes a limited number of primary feature maps using ordinary convolution, then generates additional maps through inexpensive linear operations such as depthwise transformations. These maps are concatenated to form the full output. Ghost bottlenecks combine paired Ghost modules, optional depthwise downsampling, and residual shortcuts. This replaces expensive dense convolution with a mixture of conventional and cheap feature-generation operations.

records.title: RepVGG: Making VGG-style ConvNets Great Again
records.methodology_paraphrase:
RepVGG: Making VGG-style ConvNets Great Again

During training, each RepVGG block contains multiple parallel branches, typically a 3×3 convolution, a 1×1 convolution, and an identity path, each followed by normalization. These branches improve optimization in a residual-like manner. Before deployment, the parameters of the parallel branches are algebraically fused into a single 3×3 convolution with bias. The inference graph therefore becomes a simple VGG-style stack of plain convolutions and nonlinearities with no multi-branch overhead, combining training-time structural richness with deployment-time simplicity.

records.title: EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training
records.methodology_paraphrase:
EfficientNetV2: Smaller Models and Faster Training

EfficientNetV2 redesigns the earlier compound-scaled family around training speed as well as parameter efficiency. Early stages use fused MBConv blocks that replace separate expansion and depthwise operations with regular convolution when this is faster on accelerators, while later stages retain MBConv with squeeze-and-excitation. The architecture is selected with a training-aware search objective, and progressive learning gradually increases image size and regularization strength during training. These choices shorten optimization time while maintaining strong accuracy across model scales.

records.title: High-Performance Large-Scale Image Recognition Without Normalization
records.methodology_paraphrase:
High-Performance Large-Scale Image Recognition Without Normalization

Normalizer-Free Networks remove batch normalization and instead control signal propagation analytically through residual scaling and carefully parameterized convolutions. Scaled Weight Standardization is applied to convolutional weights, and residual branches are multiplied by coefficients chosen to keep activation variance stable as depth increases. Adaptive Gradient Clipping is used to stabilize large-batch training. The block design also incorporates squeeze-and-excitation and efficient bottlenecks. This methodology demonstrates that very deep image networks can be trained competitively without activation normalization layers.

records.title: Res2Net: A New Multi-scale Backbone Architecture
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Res2Net: A New Multi-scale Backbone Architecture

A Res2Net block splits the feature channels after an initial 1×1 convolution into several smaller groups. Instead of processing all groups independently, later groups receive both their own features and the output from the previous group before applying a 3×3 convolution. The hierarchical residual-like connections within a single block create receptive fields at multiple scales. The processed groups are concatenated and projected back through a 1×1 convolution. This adds fine-grained multi-scale representation capability without requiring separate network stages or image pyramids.

records.title: Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Xception: Deep Learning with Depthwise Separable Convolutions

Xception interprets the Inception idea as an extreme separation between spatial correlation and cross-channel correlation. Each major block applies depthwise spatial convolution independently to each channel, followed by pointwise 1×1 convolution to mix channels. These depthwise separable operations are arranged in entry, middle, and exit flows with residual connections around repeated blocks. By completely decoupling spatial filtering from channel mixing, the model increases parameter efficiency while retaining a deep residual architecture suitable for large-scale image classification.

records.title: Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet and the Impact of Residual Connections on Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Inception-v4, Inception-ResNet and the Impact of Residual Connections on Learning

The Inception-v4 family standardizes the stem, reduction, and repeated Inception modules into a deeper and more uniform architecture. Parallel convolutional branches capture multiple spatial scales, while reduction modules change feature-map size between stages. The same paper also studies Inception-ResNet variants in which the concatenated branch output is projected and added to the block input through a residual connection. Residual scaling is used in very wide modules to stabilize training. The methodology explores how multi-branch Inception processing and residual optimization can be combined.

records.title: Learning Transferable Architectures for Scalable Image Recognition
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Learning Transferable Architectures for Scalable Image Recognition

The method uses reinforcement-learning-based neural architecture search to discover two reusable cell types: a Normal Cell that preserves spatial resolution and a Reduction Cell that downsamples. A controller RNN chooses pairs of hidden states and candidate operations to construct a directed acyclic computation graph. Once the cell structures are learned on a smaller proxy dataset, they are stacked repeatedly and scaled in depth and width for larger image tasks. This separates local architecture discovery from global network scaling and enables transfer of the discovered topology.

records.title: Regularized Evolution for Image Classifier Architecture Search
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Regularized Evolution for Image Classifier Architecture Search

AmoebaNet is obtained by evolutionary neural architecture search over convolutional cell structures. A population of candidate architectures is trained for a limited budget, and at each step a small tournament selects a parent while the oldest model in the sampled set is removed. The parent cell is mutated by changing an operation or connection, producing a child that is evaluated and added to the population. This aging evolution strategy regularizes the search process and discovers transferable Normal and Reduction cells that can be scaled into larger classifiers.

records.title: MnasNet: Platform-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Mobile
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MnasNet: Platform-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Mobile

The architecture is discovered using a multi-objective search that directly incorporates measured mobile-device latency instead of relying only on FLOPs. A controller samples hierarchical CNN configurations, including block types, kernel sizes, expansion ratios, and repetition counts across stages. Each sampled model receives a reward combining validation accuracy with real hardware latency. The resulting network uses inverted residual bottlenecks and depthwise convolutions but allows heterogeneous block choices across stages, producing a mobile architecture tailored to a target device and latency budget.

records.title: FBNet: Hardware-Aware Efficient ConvNet Design via Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
records.methodology_paraphrase:
FBNet: Hardware-Aware Efficient ConvNet Design via Differentiable Neural Architecture Search

FBNet formulates mobile architecture search as a differentiable optimization problem over a layer-wise supernet. Each layer contains multiple candidate operations, and continuous architecture parameters weight the candidates using a soft relaxation. The loss combines task accuracy with a differentiable latency term obtained from a hardware lookup table. Joint gradient-based optimization updates both network weights and architecture parameters, after which the highest-probability operations are selected to form the final model. This avoids expensive reinforcement-learning search while remaining hardware aware.

records.title: ProxylessNAS: Direct Neural Architecture Search on Target Task and Hardware
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ProxylessNAS: Direct Neural Architecture Search on Target Task and Hardware

ProxylessNAS searches directly on the target dataset and hardware without training a smaller proxy network. The supernet contains multiple candidate paths per layer, but binary gates activate only a small subset of paths during each update to control memory. Architecture parameters are optimized jointly with network weights, while a latency regularization term can be computed from real measurements or a predictor. The final architecture is obtained by choosing the strongest operation at each decision point, enabling device-specific networks without a proxy-task gap.

records.title: Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Once-for-All: Train One Network and Specialize it for Efficient Deployment

A single over-parameterized supernet is trained to support many sub-networks with different depths, widths, kernel sizes, and input resolutions. Progressive shrinking is used: the largest network is trained first, then increasingly smaller architectural choices are activated while sharing the inherited weights. At deployment time, an evolutionary search selects a sub-network satisfying the target device's latency or energy constraint, and no additional training is required. The approach amortizes architecture search and model training across a large family of deployment configurations.

records.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation

The architecture consists of a contracting encoder and a symmetric expanding decoder. The encoder repeatedly applies convolutional blocks followed by downsampling to capture context, while the decoder upsamples features and concatenates them with corresponding high-resolution encoder activations through skip connections. These lateral connections restore fine spatial details that would otherwise be lost during pooling. A final 1×1 convolution maps decoder features to per-pixel class scores. The design is trained end-to-end from annotated images and uses heavy augmentation to work effectively with limited segmentation data.

records.title: UNet++: A Nested U-Net Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
UNet++: A Nested U-Net Architecture for Medical Image Segmentation

UNet++ redesigns the skip pathways between encoder and decoder using a nested set of intermediate convolutional nodes. Instead of directly concatenating an encoder feature with a decoder feature at the same scale, the network progressively refines features along dense skip paths so that the semantic gap between the two sides is reduced. Deep supervision can be applied at several decoder depths, allowing outputs from different levels to contribute to training or inference. The resulting architecture preserves the multi-scale encoder-decoder structure while making feature fusion more gradual and semantically aligned.

records.title: Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Attention U-Net: Learning Where to Look for the Pancreas

Attention gates are inserted into U-Net skip connections to suppress irrelevant encoder activations before they are fused with decoder features. Each gate receives a high-resolution encoder feature and a coarser gating signal from the decoder, projects both into a shared embedding space, combines them, and predicts spatial attention coefficients. These coefficients multiply the encoder feature map so that only task-relevant regions are passed to the decoder. The gates are trained jointly with the segmentation network and add soft spatial selection without requiring an external localization model.

records.title: SegNet: A Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Architecture for Image Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SegNet: A Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Architecture for Image Segmentation

SegNet uses a convolutional encoder that follows the VGG-style hierarchy and a decoder that mirrors each encoder stage. During max pooling, the encoder stores only the pooling indices rather than the full feature maps. The decoder upsamples its lower-resolution input by placing values at the recorded pooling locations, producing sparse high-resolution maps that are then densified by convolution. This index-based unpooling reduces memory relative to storing encoder activations while preserving boundary information for dense pixel classification.

records.title: Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Fully Convolutional Networks for Semantic Segmentation

The method converts classification CNNs into dense predictors by replacing fully connected layers with convolutional layers so that the network can accept arbitrary image sizes and produce spatial score maps. Coarse deep predictions are upsampled using learnable deconvolution, and skip connections combine semantic information from deep layers with finer spatial detail from earlier pooling stages. The entire network is trained end-to-end with a pixel-wise objective. This formulation establishes fully convolutional processing as a general approach to semantic segmentation.

records.title: Encoder-Decoder with Atrous Separable Convolution for Semantic Image Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Encoder-Decoder with Atrous Separable Convolution for Semantic Image Segmentation

DeepLabv3+ combines atrous spatial pyramid pooling with an explicit encoder-decoder refinement path. The encoder uses atrous convolution at multiple dilation rates to collect context over several receptive-field sizes without reducing feature resolution excessively. A low-level feature from an early backbone stage is projected and concatenated with the upsampled high-level encoder output in the decoder, where depthwise separable convolutions refine object boundaries. This design integrates multi-scale contextual reasoning with efficient high-resolution reconstruction.

records.title: Pyramid Scene Parsing Network
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Pyramid Scene Parsing Network

The network augments a convolutional backbone with a pyramid pooling module that aggregates context over several spatial grid sizes. The final feature map is pooled into multiple coarse resolutions, each pooled representation is projected with a convolution and upsampled back to the original feature resolution, and all branches are concatenated with the local feature map. A classifier then predicts dense labels from the fused representation. The methodology explicitly injects global and regional scene context so that ambiguous local pixels can be interpreted using information from the entire image.

records.title: Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Feature Pyramid Networks for Object Detection

Feature Pyramid Networks construct a multi-scale feature hierarchy from a standard bottom-up convolutional backbone. A top-down pathway progressively upsamples semantically strong deep features, while lateral 1×1 connections merge them with corresponding higher-resolution backbone features. A 3×3 convolution produces the final feature map at each pyramid level. Detection heads can then operate at all levels using shared parameters, assigning objects of different sizes to appropriate resolutions. The key idea is to create semantically rich features at every scale without computing separate image pyramids.

records.title: Path Aggregation Network for Instance Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Path Aggregation Network for Instance Segmentation

PANet extends a feature pyramid by adding a bottom-up path augmentation after the usual top-down fusion. This shorter information route allows precise localization signals from lower backbone layers to reach high-level pyramid features more directly. The method also introduces adaptive feature pooling, which gathers candidate-region features from every pyramid level rather than assigning each proposal to a single level. A fully connected fusion branch complements mask prediction. Together these components improve information flow between low-level spatial features and high-level semantic representations.

records.title: Mask R-CNN
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mask R-CNN

Mask R-CNN extends Faster R-CNN with a parallel branch that predicts a binary segmentation mask for each detected object. The region proposal network first generates candidate boxes, and RoIAlign then samples backbone features at precisely aligned floating-point locations without the quantization used by RoIPool. Separate heads perform classification, bounding-box regression, and per-class mask prediction. The mask branch is fully convolutional and is trained with a pixel-wise loss independently of the classification score, allowing instance segmentation to be added to a two-stage detector with minimal architectural change.

records.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks

The method replaces external proposal algorithms with a Region Proposal Network that shares convolutional features with the detector. A small sliding network predicts objectness scores and bounding-box offsets for multiple anchors at every spatial location. High-scoring proposals are passed through RoI pooling and then classified and refined by the Fast R-CNN detection head. The proposal and detection components are trained with closely coupled objectives and shared backbone computation, enabling a unified two-stage detector in which proposal generation becomes part of the learned network.

records.title: R-FCN: Object Detection via Region-based Fully Convolutional Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
R-FCN: Object Detection via Region-based Fully Convolutional Networks

R-FCN makes almost all detection computation fully convolutional by generating position-sensitive score maps over the whole image. For each object class, the network predicts a bank of maps corresponding to relative spatial bins inside a candidate region. Position-sensitive RoI pooling selects and averages the appropriate bin-specific responses for each proposal, preserving translation variance needed for localization while sharing expensive convolutional computation across regions. Only lightweight aggregation is performed per proposal, reducing the cost of the region-wise head used by earlier two-stage detectors.

records.title: YOLOv3: An Incremental Improvement
records.methodology_paraphrase:
YOLOv3: An Incremental Improvement

YOLOv3 predicts bounding boxes and class scores densely at three feature-map resolutions using a single feed-forward network. Each prediction location outputs offsets relative to predefined anchor boxes, an objectness score, and independent logistic class probabilities. The backbone uses residual blocks in Darknet-53, while a feature-pyramid-like pathway combines deep semantic features with higher-resolution features for multi-scale detection. Training assigns ground-truth objects to anchors based on overlap, and inference applies confidence filtering and non-maximum suppression to the dense predictions.

records.title: Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection

RetinaNet is a one-stage detector built on a ResNet-FPN backbone with two small fully convolutional subnetworks applied independently at every pyramid level: one predicts object classes and the other predicts anchor-box regression offsets. The key methodological change is focal loss, which multiplies the standard cross-entropy by a factor that suppresses the contribution of easy, well-classified negatives. This reweighting addresses the extreme foreground-background imbalance encountered by dense detectors, allowing a simple one-stage architecture to train effectively without proposal filtering.

records.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers

DETR formulates object detection as direct set prediction. A CNN backbone produces image features that are flattened and processed by a Transformer encoder, while a fixed number of learned object queries are decoded through cross-attention. Each query predicts either one object class and bounding box or a no-object label. Training uses bipartite Hungarian matching to establish a one-to-one assignment between predictions and ground truth, followed by classification and box losses. This removes hand-designed anchors and non-maximum suppression from the detection pipeline.

records.title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection

The method replaces dense global attention over all image positions with deformable attention that samples only a small set of learned key locations around reference points. Multi-scale feature maps from the backbone are fed to the Transformer, and each query attends to sparse sampling points across several scales. Reference points are iteratively refined as boxes are updated. This sparse spatial attention reduces computation, improves convergence speed, and makes DETR substantially better at handling small objects while preserving end-to-end set prediction and Hungarian matching.

records.title: DAB-DETR: Dynamic Anchor Boxes are Better Queries for DETR
records.methodology_paraphrase:
DAB-DETR: Dynamic Anchor Boxes are Better Queries for DETR

Instead of representing decoder queries only as abstract learned vectors, DAB-DETR explicitly parameterizes each query as a four-dimensional anchor box together with content features. These box coordinates provide positional information for cross-attention and are updated layer by layer. The decoder therefore performs iterative anchor refinement while using content embeddings to identify objects. By making spatial priors explicit in the query representation, the method improves optimization and convergence without reintroducing hand-crafted proposal generation or post-hoc suppression.

records.title: Conditional DETR for Fast Training Convergence
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Conditional DETR for Fast Training Convergence

Conditional DETR decomposes each decoder query into content and spatial components and constructs a conditional spatial query for every decoder layer. Cross-attention is guided toward a localized region around a reference point rather than attending uniformly over the entire feature map. The reference location is updated as decoding proceeds, while content queries preserve object identity information. This conditional formulation narrows the spatial search space and accelerates training convergence relative to standard DETR while keeping the same end-to-end matching objective.

records.title: DN-DETR: Accelerate DETR Training by Introducing Query DeNoising
records.methodology_paraphrase:
DN-DETR: Accelerate DETR Training by Introducing Query DeNoising

The method augments DETR training with a denoising task. Ground-truth labels and boxes are deliberately corrupted and converted into additional decoder queries, and the network is trained to reconstruct the original targets from these noisy queries. Attention masks prevent denoising queries from leaking information to the ordinary matching queries. This auxiliary reconstruction signal provides direct supervision to the decoder from the beginning of training, reduces instability caused by bipartite matching, and greatly accelerates convergence without changing the inference procedure.

records.title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection

DINO combines several improvements to DETR-style detection. It uses contrastive denoising queries built from perturbed ground-truth boxes and labels, mixed query selection that initializes content and anchor information from encoder features, and look-forward-twice box refinement so later decoder layers can benefit from gradients through future refinements. The detector uses deformable multi-scale attention and iterative anchor updates. These components strengthen query initialization and optimization while retaining one-to-one matching and end-to-end detection.

records.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows

Swin Transformer computes self-attention within non-overlapping local windows rather than globally over the whole image. Consecutive blocks shift the window partition so that tokens from neighboring windows can interact. Patch-merging layers progressively reduce spatial resolution and increase channel dimension, creating a hierarchical pyramid analogous to a CNN backbone. Relative position bias is used inside each window. The architecture therefore achieves linear complexity with respect to image size and naturally produces multi-scale features suitable for classification, detection, and segmentation.

records.title: Pyramid Vision Transformer: A Versatile Backbone for Dense Prediction without Convolutions
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Pyramid Vision Transformer: A Versatile Backbone for Dense Prediction without Convolutions

PVT adapts Transformers to dense vision by building a multi-stage pyramid. Patch embeddings are generated at progressively lower spatial resolutions, and each stage contains Transformer blocks operating at a different scale. Spatial-reduction attention compresses key and value tokens before attention is computed, reducing the quadratic cost at high resolution. The resulting hierarchy produces feature maps analogous to CNN pyramids and can directly replace convolutional backbones in detection and segmentation systems.

records.title: CvT: Introducing Convolutions to Vision Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CvT: Introducing Convolutions to Vision Transformers

CvT introduces convolutional projections into the Transformer pipeline. Each stage first embeds the image with a convolutional tokenization layer, then computes queries, keys, and values using depthwise separable convolutions rather than plain linear projections. Stages progressively reduce spatial resolution and increase feature dimension, producing a hierarchical representation. These convolutional projections inject locality, translation-related inductive bias, and spatial downsampling while preserving the global self-attention mechanism, allowing the model to combine convolutional structure with Transformer flexibility.

records.title: Training Data-Efficient Image Transformers & Distillation through Attention
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Training Data-Efficient Image Transformers & Distillation through Attention

DeiT retains the ViT architecture but develops a training recipe that enables strong performance using ImageNet-scale data rather than extremely large pre-training corpora. The method uses heavy augmentation, regularization, and optimization choices tailored to Transformers. It also introduces a distillation token processed alongside the class token and patch tokens. This token is trained to match predictions from a teacher network, allowing knowledge distillation to occur through attention inside the Transformer instead of only through an output-level loss.

records.title: Tokens-to-Token ViT: Training Vision Transformers from Scratch on ImageNet
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Tokens-to-Token ViT: Training Vision Transformers from Scratch on ImageNet

Tokens-to-Token ViT replaces the single rigid patch partition with a progressive tokenization process. Neighboring image patches are repeatedly restructured and softly aggregated so that local visual patterns such as edges and textures are encoded before the main Transformer backbone. The resulting tokens contain richer local structure and fewer isolated patch boundaries. A compact deep-narrow Transformer then processes these tokens globally. The methodology aims to improve sample efficiency by introducing local image inductive bias without reverting to a conventional convolutional backbone.

records.title: Transformer in Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Transformer in Transformer

TNT models an image at two nested granularities. Each image patch is treated as a visual sentence containing smaller pixel-level tokens. An inner Transformer updates the pixel tokens within each patch, and their aggregated representation is projected into the corresponding patch token. An outer Transformer then performs self-attention across patch tokens to model global relationships. This alternating inner-outer computation lets the network explicitly capture fine local structure inside patches while simultaneously learning long-range interactions between patches.

records.title: Going Deeper with Image Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Going Deeper with Image Transformers

CaiT stabilizes very deep vision Transformers using two main modifications. LayerScale introduces small learnable scaling coefficients on residual branches so that deep blocks begin close to the identity mapping and become expressive gradually during training. Class-attention blocks are moved to the end of the network: patch tokens are first processed without a class token, then a small set of dedicated blocks lets the class token attend to the frozen patch-token set. This separates spatial representation learning from final class aggregation and supports much deeper architectures.

records.title: Rethinking Spatial Dimensions of Vision Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Rethinking Spatial Dimensions of Vision Transformers

PiT introduces a pooling mechanism into Vision Transformers so that token resolution decreases across stages while channel dimension grows. After several Transformer blocks, a depthwise convolution-based pooling layer reduces the spatial token grid and projects features to a higher-dimensional representation. A class token is propagated through corresponding projections. The resulting hierarchical architecture mimics the scale progression of CNNs while retaining self-attention within each stage, improving both computational efficiency and compatibility with multi-scale visual representations.

records.title: LeViT: a Vision Transformer in ConvNet's Clothing for Faster Inference
records.methodology_paraphrase:
LeViT: a Vision Transformer in ConvNet's Clothing for Faster Inference

LeViT is designed around fast image classification on practical hardware. A small convolutional stem quickly downsamples the input and produces tokens, after which attention blocks operate at progressively lower resolutions. The architecture removes expensive normalization choices, uses attention bias tables for relative positions, and employs shrinking attention blocks to reduce token count between stages. The network is trained with knowledge distillation and combines convolutional early processing with efficient Transformer stages to achieve high throughput at low latency.

records.title: CoAtNet: Marrying Convolution and Attention for All Data Sizes
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CoAtNet: Marrying Convolution and Attention for All Data Sizes

CoAtNet constructs a stage-wise hierarchy that begins with convolutional blocks and transitions to relative self-attention blocks at deeper levels. The design interprets depthwise convolution and attention through a shared formulation, using convolution where local inductive bias and generalization are beneficial and attention where global receptive fields and model capacity become more important. Spatial resolution is reduced between stages while channel width grows. This hybrid schedule allows the same family to perform well from moderate-scale datasets to very large pre-training regimes.

records.title: MaxViT: Multi-Axis Vision Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MaxViT: Multi-Axis Vision Transformer

Each MaxViT block combines three operations: an MBConv convolutional block, block attention within non-overlapping local windows, and grid attention across a sparse global grid. The local attention captures short-range structure efficiently, while grid attention allows information to travel globally without full quadratic attention over all pixels. The block is stacked in a hierarchical multi-stage backbone with downsampling between stages. This multi-axis attention pattern gives every token access to both local context and global interactions while preserving favorable computational scaling.

records.title: Focal Modulation Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Focal Modulation Networks

FocalNet replaces self-attention with a focal modulation operator. A hierarchy of depthwise convolutions aggregates context at multiple receptive-field sizes, and a learned gating mechanism weights these contextual levels for each position. The aggregated context is transformed into a modulator that multiplicatively conditions the local token representation. Because interactions are mediated through aggregated context rather than pairwise token attention, the operator scales linearly with sequence length while still supporting adaptive multi-scale contextual reasoning in hierarchical vision backbones.

records.title: Twins: Revisiting the Design of Spatial Attention in Vision Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Twins: Revisiting the Design of Spatial Attention in Vision Transformers

Twins combines local and global spatial attention in alternating blocks. Locally-grouped self-attention partitions the feature map into sub-windows and performs dense attention only within each group, reducing computation. Global sub-sampled attention then lets every query attend to a spatially downsampled set of keys and values, providing long-range communication at lower cost. These blocks are arranged in a pyramid with progressive downsampling. The method therefore balances local detail, global context, and efficiency without relying on shifted windows.

records.title: CrossViT: Cross-Attention Multi-Scale Vision Transformer for Image Classification
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CrossViT: Cross-Attention Multi-Scale Vision Transformer for Image Classification

CrossViT processes the same image with two Transformer branches using different patch sizes. The small-patch branch preserves fine local detail, while the large-patch branch captures coarse global structure with fewer tokens. At fusion points, the class token from one branch attends to patch tokens from the other through cross-attention, and the information exchange is performed in both directions. This avoids concatenating all tokens into one expensive sequence and allows the model to combine complementary spatial scales efficiently.

records.title: MobileViT: Light-weight, General-purpose, and Mobile-friendly Vision Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MobileViT: Light-weight, General-purpose, and Mobile-friendly Vision Transformer

A MobileViT block first applies local convolutions to encode neighborhood features, unfolds the resulting feature map into small non-overlapping patches, and applies Transformer layers across corresponding positions to capture global relationships. The Transformer output is folded back to the spatial grid, projected with convolution, and fused with the original local feature map. This creates a lightweight unit that combines CNN locality with global token interaction while preserving the spatially structured representation and deployment characteristics needed for mobile vision.

records.title: MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MLP-Mixer: An all-MLP Architecture for Vision

The image is split into patches and projected into a sequence of token embeddings, but no attention or convolution is used after tokenization. Each Mixer block alternates two MLPs: a token-mixing MLP operates across spatial tokens independently for every channel, and a channel-mixing MLP operates across channels independently for every token. Residual connections and normalization surround both transformations. Repeating these blocks allows global spatial communication and feature transformation using only matrix multiplications and element-wise nonlinearities.

records.title: Pay Attention to MLPs
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Pay Attention to MLPs

gMLP uses stacked MLP blocks in which channel projections are combined with a Spatial Gating Unit. After an initial channel expansion, the representation is split into two parts; one part is linearly projected across the sequence dimension after normalization and then multiplied element-wise with the other part. This learned spatial projection provides token interaction without self-attention. Residual connections and feed-forward channel transformations complete the block. The approach shows that multiplicative spatial gating can serve as an effective alternative to attention in sequence models.

records.title: ResMLP: Feedforward Networks for Image Classification with Data-Efficient Training
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ResMLP: Feedforward Networks for Image Classification with Data-Efficient Training

ResMLP treats an image as a set of patch embeddings and repeatedly applies two residual transformations. The first mixes information across patches using a learned linear layer shared across channels; the second applies an MLP across feature channels independently for each patch. Affine normalization replaces LayerNorm, and learnable residual scaling stabilizes deep networks. The architecture contains neither convolution nor self-attention after patch embedding, relying entirely on linear token mixing and channel MLPs to build global visual representations.

records.title: Patches Are All You Need?
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Patches Are All You Need?

ConvMixer begins by embedding non-overlapping image patches with a strided convolution. Each repeated block then applies a depthwise convolution across the spatial grid, followed by activation and normalization, adds a residual connection, and uses a pointwise 1×1 convolution to mix channels. The architecture therefore separates spatial mixing from channel mixing in a way analogous to token- and channel-mixing MLPs, but uses convolutional operators. Large kernels allow broad spatial interaction while preserving a simple isotropic feature dimension throughout the network.

records.title: MetaFormer is Actually What You Need for Vision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MetaFormer is Actually What You Need for Vision

MetaFormer abstracts modern vision backbones into a common skeleton containing normalization, a token-mixing operator, residual connections, and a channel MLP. The paper argues that much of the effectiveness comes from this macro-architecture rather than from self-attention itself. By replacing attention with very simple token mixers such as pooling while keeping the same residual-and-MLP structure, the authors show that strong performance can still be obtained. The framework therefore separates the architectural scaffold from the specific mechanism used to exchange information among tokens.

records.title: MetaFormer is Actually What You Need for Vision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MetaFormer is Actually What You Need for Vision

PoolFormer instantiates the MetaFormer framework using a parameter-free pooling operator as the token mixer. Each block normalizes the input, computes a local average-pooled feature, subtracts the original feature to obtain a mixing signal, and adds the result through a residual path. A second residual branch applies a channel MLP. The network is organized hierarchically with patch embeddings and spatial downsampling between stages. The simplicity of the pooling mixer is used to demonstrate the strength of the surrounding MetaFormer architecture.

records.title: FNet: Mixing Tokens with Fourier Transforms
records.methodology_paraphrase:
FNet: Mixing Tokens with Fourier Transforms

FNet replaces the self-attention sublayer of a Transformer encoder with an unparameterized two-dimensional Fourier transform applied across the sequence and hidden dimensions. The real component of the transformed representation is combined with the original input through a residual connection, followed by the usual feed-forward network, normalization, and another residual connection. Because the Fourier transform mixes information globally with low computational overhead, the architecture retains the Transformer block structure while eliminating learned pairwise attention weights.

records.title: Synthesizer: Rethinking Self-Attention for Transformer Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Synthesizer: Rethinking Self-Attention for Transformer Models

Synthesizer replaces dot-product attention scores with alternatives that do not depend on pairwise query-key similarity. In the dense variant, a feed-forward network directly generates attention-like mixing weights from each token. In the random variant, the token-mixing matrix is learned as a free parameter independent of the input. These matrices are normalized and used to combine value vectors in the same structural position where self-attention would normally appear. The experiments isolate how much Transformer performance depends on content-based attention versus generic learned token mixing.

records.title: Attention Is All You Need
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Attention Is All You Need

The Transformer is an encoder-decoder sequence architecture built entirely from attention and feed-forward layers. Multi-head self-attention projects each token into queries, keys, and values, computes scaled dot-product attention in several parallel subspaces, and concatenates the results. The decoder additionally uses masked self-attention and encoder-decoder cross-attention. Position-wise feed-forward networks, residual connections, and layer normalization are applied in every block. Because recurrence is removed, sequence positions can be processed in parallel while attention provides direct paths between distant tokens.

records.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

BERT uses a stack of Transformer encoder layers to learn deep bidirectional token representations. Pre-training is driven by masked language modeling, where a subset of input tokens is hidden or corrupted and the model predicts their identities using both left and right context. The original formulation also includes next-sentence prediction over paired segments. Segment embeddings, positional embeddings, and token embeddings are summed at the input. The same pre-trained encoder is then fine-tuned with small task-specific heads for classification, tagging, or span prediction.

records.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
records.methodology_paraphrase:
RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

RoBERTa keeps the BERT encoder architecture but revises the pre-training procedure. It removes the next-sentence prediction objective, trains substantially longer on more data with larger effective batches, and uses dynamically generated masking patterns rather than a single static mask. Longer input sequences are used more consistently, and optimization settings are retuned for scale. The methodology is intentionally architectural conservative: the contribution is to show that careful data construction, masking, and training configuration can yield large gains without changing the Transformer encoder itself.

records.title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations

ALBERT reduces the parameter cost of BERT through two factorization strategies. The vocabulary embedding matrix is decomposed into a smaller embedding dimension followed by a projection to the hidden size, and Transformer parameters are shared across layers rather than independently allocated at each depth. The pre-training objective replaces next-sentence prediction with sentence-order prediction, which asks the model to distinguish correctly ordered consecutive segments from swapped ones. These changes enable much larger hidden representations and deeper models under a controlled parameter budget.

records.title: ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ELECTRA: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators

ELECTRA trains two Transformer networks jointly. A small generator performs masked language modeling and proposes plausible replacements for masked tokens. The corrupted sequence is then passed to a discriminator, which predicts at every position whether the observed token is original or generator-produced. Because the discriminator receives a learning signal for nearly every token rather than only masked positions, pre-training is more sample efficient. After pre-training, the generator is discarded and the discriminator encoder is fine-tuned on downstream language tasks.

records.title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding
records.methodology_paraphrase:
XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining for Language Understanding

XLNet uses permutation language modeling to learn bidirectional context while retaining an autoregressive likelihood objective. During training, the factorization order of tokens is randomly permuted, so a token may be predicted using context from positions that would lie on both sides in the original sequence. A two-stream attention mechanism separates content representations from query representations to prevent the target token from being revealed. The architecture is built on Transformer-XL recurrence, allowing hidden states from previous segments to provide longer contextual history.

records.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

Transformer-XL introduces segment-level recurrence to reuse hidden states from preceding text segments. Cached activations from the previous segment are concatenated with the current segment when computing keys and values, extending the effective context without backpropagating through the entire history. A relative positional encoding formulation replaces absolute positions so that attention remains consistent when memory from different segments is reused. This recurrent memory mechanism addresses context fragmentation and enables substantially longer dependency modeling than fixed-window Transformers.

records.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

T5 casts every task into a text-to-text format: the input is a text sequence describing the task and content, and the target is another text sequence. The model uses a standard Transformer encoder-decoder architecture with relative position bias. Pre-training applies a span-corruption objective in which contiguous token spans are replaced by sentinel tokens and the decoder reconstructs the missing spans in sequence. Classification, translation, summarization, question answering, and other tasks are all fine-tuned using the same sequence generation interface.

records.title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training for Natural Language Generation, Translation, and Comprehension

BART combines a bidirectional Transformer encoder with an autoregressive Transformer decoder. During pre-training, clean text is corrupted by noise functions such as token masking, token deletion, text infilling, sentence permutation, and document rotation. The encoder reads the corrupted sequence and the decoder reconstructs the original text from left to right. This denoising autoencoding objective gives the encoder strong bidirectional representations while preserving a decoder specialized for generation, enabling one architecture to support both understanding and sequence generation tasks.

records.title: DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention
records.methodology_paraphrase:
DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention

DeBERTa separates each token representation into content and position components and computes attention using disentangled interactions between content-content, content-position, and position-content terms. Relative positions are therefore modeled directly inside attention rather than added only once to token embeddings. The paper also introduces an enhanced mask decoder that incorporates absolute position information near the output when reconstructing masked tokens. These modifications preserve the BERT-style encoder and masked-language objective while providing a richer representation of positional relationships.

records.title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer

Longformer replaces full self-attention with a sparse pattern designed for long sequences. Most tokens use a sliding local attention window, giving linear complexity with document length. A small set of task-dependent tokens can be assigned global attention, allowing them to attend to every position and be attended to by all positions. This combination supports local contextual modeling throughout the document while preserving direct long-range communication through selected global tokens. The architecture can be initialized from a standard pre-trained Transformer and extended to much longer inputs.

records.title: Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Big Bird: Transformers for Longer Sequences

BigBird constructs a sparse attention graph that combines three connection types: local sliding-window attention, random attention to a small subset of tokens, and global attention involving designated tokens. This pattern reduces the quadratic attention matrix to linear complexity while maintaining broad information flow. The paper analyzes the expressiveness of the sparse graph and shows that it preserves key theoretical properties associated with full attention. The architecture is then used for long-document language modeling and question answering with substantially longer contexts than dense Transformers.

records.title: Reformer: The Efficient Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Reformer: The Efficient Transformer

Reformer reduces memory and compute through two main mechanisms. Locality-sensitive hashing attention groups queries and keys into hash buckets so that attention is computed mainly among similar vectors rather than across all token pairs. Reversible residual layers reconstruct intermediate activations during backpropagation instead of storing them, lowering memory usage. The feed-forward layer is processed in chunks to further control memory. Together these changes allow Transformer-style models to operate on much longer sequences under limited hardware resources.

records.title: Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Linformer: Self-Attention with Linear Complexity

Linformer assumes that the attention matrix can be well approximated by a low-rank structure. Before dot-product attention is computed, the key and value sequences are projected from the original sequence length into a much smaller fixed dimension using learned linear projection matrices. Queries remain at full length, so the resulting attention computation scales linearly rather than quadratically with the number of tokens. The projection can be shared across heads or layers, making the modification easy to insert into standard Transformer blocks.

records.title: Rethinking Attention with Performers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Rethinking Attention with Performers

Performer approximates softmax attention using FAVOR+, a random-feature method that rewrites the attention kernel as an inner product of positive feature maps. Queries and keys are transformed independently, allowing the associative order of matrix multiplication to be changed so that the full token-by-token attention matrix never needs to be formed. Orthogonal random features reduce estimator variance. The resulting attention layer has linear time and memory complexity in sequence length while approximating standard softmax attention without imposing a fixed sparsity pattern.

records.title: Nyströmformer: A Nyström-Based Algorithm for Approximating Self-Attention
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Nyströmformer: A Nyström-Based Algorithm for Approximating Self-Attention

Nyströmformer approximates the full self-attention matrix using the Nyström method. Tokens are summarized into a smaller set of landmark representations, and attention is computed between tokens and landmarks as well as among landmarks. A fast iterative approximation to the pseudoinverse reconstructs an estimate of the original attention operator from these smaller matrices. Because the number of landmarks is much smaller than the sequence length, computational and memory costs are reduced while retaining a global low-rank approximation to self-attention.

records.title: Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Efficient Content-Based Sparse Attention with Routing Transformers

Routing Transformer assigns token representations to clusters in query/key space and restricts self-attention to tokens routed to the same cluster, with a local window used to preserve nearby context. The centroids are updated online so that the sparse pattern depends on content rather than fixed positions. By attending only within selected clusters, the model reduces the cost of long-sequence attention while still allowing distant but semantically related tokens to interact directly.

records.title: Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Generating Long Sequences with Sparse Transformers

The model replaces dense causal attention with structured sparse patterns so that each token attends only to selected previous positions. Strided and fixed attention layouts are arranged so information can propagate across the entire sequence through a small number of layers. The reduced attention graph allows substantially longer images, text, or audio-like sequences to be modeled autoregressively while preserving Transformer-style parallel training and direct long-range paths.

records.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity

Switch Transformer replaces the dense feed-forward sublayer with a sparse mixture-of-experts module. A learned router sends each token to a single expert network, so model capacity can grow dramatically while the per-token computation remains close to a dense Transformer. Auxiliary load-balancing losses prevent expert collapse, and expert capacity limits control routing overflow. The rest of the Transformer remains conventional, making sparse expert scaling a drop-in modification to the feed-forward path.

records.title: GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts
records.methodology_paraphrase:
GLaM: Efficient Scaling of Language Models with Mixture-of-Experts

GLaM inserts sparsely activated expert feed-forward layers into a Transformer. For each token, a learned gating network selects a small number of experts from a much larger pool, and only those expert MLPs are evaluated. Dense attention layers remain shared across all tokens. Load balancing and capacity constraints distribute traffic across experts. This conditional computation lets the total parameter count grow far faster than active computation, enabling very large language models with lower training and inference cost per token.

records.title: Mixtral of Experts
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mixtral of Experts

Mixtral uses a decoder-only Transformer in which each feed-forward block is replaced by a sparse mixture of experts. A router computes scores over experts for every token and activates the top two experts, whose outputs are combined using normalized routing weights. Attention remains dense and shared, while expert parameters provide additional model capacity. Because only two experts are executed for each token, the architecture increases total parameter count without increasing active computation proportionally.

records.title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens

RETRO augments an autoregressive Transformer with nearest-neighbor retrieval from a very large external text database. The training corpus is divided into chunks, embedded, and indexed. During language modeling, each chunk retrieves similar neighbors; a separate encoder processes those neighbors, and cross-attention modules inject the retrieved evidence into selected decoder layers. The base model still predicts tokens autoregressively, but factual and long-tail information can be accessed from the database rather than stored entirely in parameters.

records.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
records.methodology_paraphrase:
REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training

REALM jointly trains a neural retriever and a language model. The retriever maps an input context and candidate documents into a shared embedding space and defines a distribution over retrieved documents from a large corpus. The reader conditions masked-token predictions on each retrieved document, and the retrieval probabilities are treated as latent variables. Gradients from the language-model objective therefore update both the reader and retriever, allowing retrieval behavior to be learned without document-level supervision.

records.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

RAG combines a dense document retriever with a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence generator. The input query is embedded and used to retrieve a small set of passages from an external index. Each passage is concatenated with the input and passed to the generator, while retrieval scores define a probability distribution over documents. Generation probabilities are marginalized across retrieved evidence, either at the sequence level or token level. The model is trained end-to-end for knowledge-intensive generation without storing all facts in the generator parameters.

records.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

DPR uses two independent BERT encoders: one maps questions into dense vectors and the other maps passages into the same space. Relevance is measured by the dot product between question and passage embeddings. Training uses positive question-passage pairs together with in-batch and hard negatives under a contrastive softmax objective. At inference, all corpus passages are pre-encoded and indexed for approximate nearest-neighbor search, allowing efficient retrieval without sparse lexical matching.

records.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

ColBERT independently encodes query and document tokens with BERT and projects them into lower-dimensional contextual embeddings. Instead of collapsing each text into a single vector, relevance is computed with late interaction: every query-token embedding selects its maximum similarity to any document-token embedding, and these maxima are summed. Document token vectors can be precomputed and indexed, preserving fine-grained token matching while avoiding expensive joint cross-encoding of every query-document pair.

records.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks

Sentence-BERT places two or three BERT encoders in a Siamese or triplet architecture with shared weights.
