Each sentence is encoded independently and pooled into a fixed-length embedding, after which cosine similarity or a classifier is used for training. Objectives based on natural-language inference, semantic similarity, or triplet ranking encourage semantically related sentences to occupy nearby regions in embedding space. Because embeddings are independent, large-scale semantic search becomes practical without pairwise cross-encoding.

records.title: Deep contextualized word representations
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Deep contextualized word representations

ELMo learns token representations from a deep bidirectional language model. A character-level convolutional encoder constructs context-independent token inputs, and stacked forward and backward LSTMs predict neighboring tokens in opposite directions. For downstream tasks, the hidden states from multiple language-model layers are combined using learned task-specific scalar weights. Each token therefore receives a context-dependent embedding whose meaning changes with the surrounding sentence while preserving lower-level syntactic and lexical information from different layers.

records.title: Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification

ULMFiT transfers a pre-trained AWD-LSTM language model to a target classification task in stages. The language model is first pre-trained on a large general corpus, then fine-tuned on unlabeled text from the target domain using discriminative learning rates and slanted triangular schedules. A classifier head is added and trained with gradual unfreezing, exposing deeper recurrent layers progressively. This procedure reduces catastrophic forgetting and allows a single language-model backbone to adapt effectively even when labeled data are limited.

records.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space

Word2Vec learns distributed word embeddings using shallow predictive models. In CBOW, surrounding context vectors are aggregated to predict a center word; in Skip-gram, the center word predicts nearby context words. Hierarchical softmax or negative sampling reduces the cost of the large vocabulary normalization. The learned embedding matrix places words with similar distributional contexts near one another and captures regularities through vector relationships, while avoiding the computational expense of deeper neural language models.

records.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

GloVe learns word vectors directly from global co-occurrence statistics. A weighted least-squares objective fits the dot product between two word embeddings, plus learned biases, to the logarithm of their corpus co-occurrence count. A weighting function limits the influence of extremely frequent or very rare pairs. The formulation is motivated by ratios of co-occurrence probabilities, so semantic relationships are encoded as linear directions in the embedding space while training remains a simple matrix-factorization-like optimization.

records.title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information

FastText extends the Skip-gram objective by representing each word as a sum of vectors associated with character n-grams and the whole word. Context prediction is performed using this composed representation, while negative sampling or hierarchical softmax provides efficient training. Because subword units are shared across related spellings, the model can infer useful vectors for rare and previously unseen words and captures morphology more directly than a lookup table containing one independent vector per vocabulary item.

records.title: LSTM: A Search Space Odyssey
records.methodology_paraphrase:
LSTM: A Search Space Odyssey

The paper takes the standard LSTM memory cell as the reference recurrent architecture and systematically studies how its gating and state-update components affect performance. The baseline contains an input gate, forget gate, output gate, candidate update, and additive cell-state pathway. Controlled variants remove or modify individual gates, change nonlinearities, alter input handling, or couple gate behavior while keeping the surrounding training setup comparable. This methodology treats LSTM not as one indivisible design, but as a structured family whose recurrent memory mechanisms can be evaluated component by component.

records.title: Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Learning Phrase Representations using RNN Encoder-Decoder for Statistical Machine Translation

The gated recurrent unit combines recurrent state control into two gates. An update gate interpolates between the previous hidden state and a newly computed candidate, while a reset gate determines how strongly past information contributes when forming that candidate. There is no separate cell state as in LSTM, producing a simpler recurrent transition. In the original encoder-decoder setting, one GRU network compresses a source sequence and another generates a target sequence conditioned on the encoded representation.

records.title: Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Quasi-Recurrent Neural Networks

QRNN separates temporal feature extraction from recurrent state pooling. Wide one-dimensional convolutions compute candidate activations and gate values for all time steps in parallel. A lightweight recurrent pooling function then combines these precomputed signals sequentially using element-wise operations such as forget or output gates. Because the expensive matrix multiplications are convolutional and parallelizable while recurrence is inexpensive, the architecture retains recurrent memory behavior with substantially higher training throughput on long sequences.

records.title: Simple Recurrent Unit: Highly Parallelizable Recurrence for Sequence Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Simple Recurrent Unit: Highly Parallelizable Recurrence for Sequence Modeling

SRU redesigns recurrence so that matrix multiplications depend only on the current input and can therefore be computed for all time steps in parallel. Recurrent dependencies are restricted to inexpensive element-wise state updates controlled by forget and reset gates. Highway-style connections combine the recurrent state with a transformed input to form the output. This separation preserves a sequential memory path while moving most computation outside the recurrence, allowing deep recurrent networks to approach Transformer-like parallel efficiency.

records.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling

The temporal convolutional network uses one-dimensional causal convolutions so that predictions at time t depend only on current and earlier inputs. Dilated convolutions expand the receptive field exponentially with depth, while residual blocks stabilize optimization. Because convolutions over a sequence can be evaluated in parallel during training, TCN avoids recurrent state updates yet can model long histories through dilation. The architecture is applied as a generic sequence model rather than being specialized to a particular domain.

records.title: Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Efficiently Modeling Long Sequences with Structured State Spaces

S4 parameterizes a continuous-time linear state-space model and discretizes it to define a long convolution kernel over sequences. A specially structured state matrix derived from HiPPO enables stable long-range memory, while diagonal-plus-low-rank algebra allows the convolution kernel to be computed efficiently. During training the layer can be implemented as a global convolution using FFT-style operations; during autoregressive inference it can be run recurrently. Stacking S4 layers with nonlinear projections yields a general long-sequence neural architecture.

records.title: Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Simplified State Space Layers for Sequence Modeling

S5 simplifies structured state-space modeling by using a single multi-input multi-output state-space layer rather than many independent single-input systems. The state matrix is diagonalized so the recurrence and parallel scan can be evaluated efficiently, while learned input and output projections mix channels. Initialization transfers the long-memory properties of HiPPO into the diagonal representation. The layer can therefore process long sequences with linear state updates and is combined with residual connections and nonlinear feed-forward transformations.

records.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

Mamba makes state-space parameters input dependent so the model can selectively retain or forget information based on the current token. A learned projection produces per-token discretization steps and state-space input/output coefficients, creating a selective recurrence that cannot be reduced to one fixed convolution kernel. A hardware-aware parallel scan computes this recurrence efficiently during training. The block combines the selective state-space operator with gating and local projection layers, achieving linear sequence scaling while preserving content-dependent dynamics.

records.title: Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality

Mamba-2 is derived through Structured State Space Duality, which expresses a family of state-space layers and attention-like operations through structured semiseparable matrices. The architecture reorganizes the selective state-space computation into a form that supports larger state dimensions and efficient matrix-multiplication kernels. Input-dependent coefficients still control the recurrence, but the implementation processes sequence chunks with a combination of intra-chunk matrix operations and compact recurrent state transfer. This improves hardware efficiency while retaining linear-time sequence modeling.

records.title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
records.methodology_paraphrase:
RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era

RWKV combines token mixing and channel mixing in residual blocks while defining the sequence interaction as a weighted key-value recurrence. The time-mixing operator can be expressed in a parallel form during training but converted into a constant-memory recurrent update at inference. Learned receptance gates control how the accumulated weighted values influence each token representation. This dual formulation preserves Transformer-like parallel optimization while allowing decoding with RNN-like O(1) memory per step and linear computational growth with context length.

records.title: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models

RetNet replaces attention with a retention mechanism that has mathematically equivalent parallel, recurrent, and chunkwise-recurrent forms. During training, retention can be evaluated over all tokens in parallel using decayed pairwise interactions. During decoding, a compact recurrent state summarizes the past and is updated in constant time. For long contexts, chunks are processed in parallel internally while summary states propagate between chunks. Multi-scale decay factors across heads provide different memory horizons inside each retention block.

records.title: Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Hyena Hierarchy: Towards Larger Convolutional Language Models

Hyena replaces attention with an operator built from long implicit convolutions and data-controlled multiplicative gates. Long filters are generated by a compact neural function rather than stored directly, allowing very large receptive fields with subquadratic computation. Several gated convolution stages are composed hierarchically so token-dependent projections modulate how information is mixed across the sequence. FFT-based convolution provides efficient training for long contexts, while the architecture avoids constructing a dense token-by-token attention matrix.

records.title: Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Hungry Hungry Hippos: Towards Language Modeling with State Space Models

H3 develops an attention-free language-modeling layer around structured state-space operators. A shift-like state-space component captures local token interactions, while a diagonal state-space component provides long-range memory. Multiplicative interactions among projected inputs create content-dependent behavior, and the entire sequence operator can be evaluated efficiently with convolution during training. H3 blocks are interleaved with feed-forward layers and can also be combined with a small number of attention layers to strengthen associative recall.

records.title: Mega: Moving Average Equipped Gated Attention
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mega: Moving Average Equipped Gated Attention

Mega combines an exponential moving-average representation with gated attention. A multi-dimensional damped moving average summarizes long sequence history in linear time and supplies position-aware contextual features. These features are used to generate queries, keys, values, and gates for an attention-like update whose effective sequence interaction can be chunked efficiently. The architecture also includes gated residual pathways and feed-forward processing. By coupling recurrence-like moving averages with attention, Mega targets long-context modeling with reduced computational cost.

records.title: Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models

Griffin alternates gated linear recurrent blocks with local multi-head attention. The recurrent component uses a data-dependent gate around a linear recurrence so that the model can summarize arbitrarily long history with constant recurrent state, while short-range attention provides precise local content interaction. The architecture is arranged so training remains highly parallelizable and inference requires less memory than global-attention Transformers. Local attention windows and recurrent states therefore divide responsibility between short-context matching and long-context memory.

records.title: Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models

Hawk is the recurrent-only architecture introduced alongside Griffin. Its core block uses a gated linear recurrence in which input projections determine candidate features, gates, and recurrent decay behavior. The recurrence is designed to admit efficient parallel training while maintaining a compact state for autoregressive inference. Feed-forward channel transformations and residual connections surround the recurrent operator. Hawk demonstrates that carefully gated linear recurrence can serve as the principal sequence-mixing mechanism without relying on full self-attention.

records.title: xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory
records.methodology_paraphrase:
xLSTM: Extended Long Short-Term Memory

xLSTM modernizes the LSTM family with two recurrent cells. sLSTM introduces exponential gating and a stabilized memory update that supports stronger state control, while mLSTM stores information in a matrix-valued memory and uses covariance-like updates to increase capacity. The cells are organized into residual blocks with projection and normalization layers, and block stacks can mix sLSTM and mLSTM in different proportions. The design keeps recurrent constant-memory inference while substantially increasing the expressive power of classical gated recurrence.

records.title: Legendre Memory Units: Continuous-Time Representation in Recurrent Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Legendre Memory Units: Continuous-Time Representation in Recurrent Neural Networks

The Legendre Memory Unit derives a recurrent memory system from a linear time-invariant state-space model that optimally represents a sliding window of recent input using coefficients of shifted Legendre polynomials. The memory state is updated by fixed matrices determined analytically, while a learned neural component uses the current input, hidden representation, and memory to produce outputs. This separates long-term temporal memory from nonlinear computation and provides a compact, structured representation of recent sequence history.

records.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

KAN replaces fixed scalar activation functions on nodes with learnable univariate functions placed on edges. Each layer computes sums of edge-wise nonlinear transformations rather than a conventional matrix multiplication followed by an element-wise activation. The edge functions are parameterized with spline bases and can be adaptively refined by extending the spline grid. The design is motivated by the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem and aims to provide more interpretable functional components while retaining end-to-end gradient-based training.

records.title: Neural Ordinary Differential Equations
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Neural Ordinary Differential Equations

Neural ODE models define hidden-state evolution through a continuous-time differential equation rather than a fixed sequence of discrete residual layers. A neural network parameterizes the derivative dh/dt, and a black-box ODE solver integrates this dynamics from the initial state to the requested time. Gradients can be computed using an adjoint sensitivity method that solves another differential equation backward in time. This formulation provides adaptive computation depth, continuous-time latent trajectories, and memory-efficient training for suitable dynamics.

records.title: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Irregular Time Series

Neural CDEs represent an observed time series as a continuous control path obtained through interpolation. A hidden state evolves according to a controlled differential equation whose vector field is parameterized by a neural network and whose increments are driven by the interpolated data path. The terminal hidden state is used for prediction. Because time enters through the control path rather than fixed sampling intervals, the architecture naturally handles irregular observations and can be viewed as a continuous-time analogue of recurrent sequence models.

records.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States

Test-Time Training layers treat part of the hidden state as the parameters of a small learner that is updated while processing the sequence. For each incoming token, the layer performs one or more gradient-based updates on a self-supervised objective, so the internal model adapts to recently observed context. The updated parameters then transform subsequent tokens. This creates a recurrent mechanism whose hidden state is itself a learnable model, increasing memory capacity beyond a fixed-size activation vector while maintaining sequential inference.

records.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time

Titans introduces a long-term neural memory module that is updated online as tokens are processed. The memory is a parameterized network rather than a simple recurrent vector, and surprise- or novelty-related signals determine which information should strongly modify it. Short-term attention handles precise local dependencies, while persistent neural memory stores information over much longer horizons. Different architectural variants integrate memory as context, as a gating component, or as an additional layer, combining fast attention with test-time adaptive storage.

records.title: Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention

Perceiver maps a potentially huge and modality-agnostic input array into a much smaller set of latent vectors using cross-attention. Computationally expensive latent self-attention is then performed only within this fixed-size latent set, and the input can be revisited through repeated cross-attention blocks. Positional or modality features are attached to raw inputs rather than requiring a domain-specific backbone. By separating input size from latent processing size, the architecture can handle images, audio, point clouds, and other high-dimensional data with controlled attention cost.

records.title: Perceiver IO: A General Architecture for Structured Inputs & Outputs
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Perceiver IO: A General Architecture for Structured Inputs & Outputs

Perceiver IO extends the latent-bottleneck architecture to arbitrary structured outputs. Inputs are first encoded into a compact latent array through cross-attention and latent self-attention. A separate set of output queries then cross-attends to the final latent representation; each query specifies what information should be decoded, such as a pixel position, class, text position, or other output element. This query-based decoder allows one common architecture to support classification, dense prediction, multimodal generation, and variable-sized outputs.

records.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

Flamingo connects a frozen vision encoder and a frozen language model through two trainable components. A Perceiver Resampler converts variable-size visual features into a fixed number of visual tokens, and gated cross-attention layers are inserted between selected language-model blocks so text representations can attend to those tokens. Interleaved image-text sequences are trained autoregressively with a language-model objective. Because most backbone weights remain frozen, the system learns multimodal few-shot behavior by training only the new visual-conditioning modules.

records.title: BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BLIP: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training for Unified Vision-Language Understanding and Generation

BLIP uses a shared vision encoder with multimodal Transformer components configured for image-text contrastive learning, image-text matching, and conditional language modeling. A captioning model generates synthetic descriptions for web images, and a filtering model removes noisy image-text pairs before pre-training. The same parameters are reused across understanding and generation configurations by changing attention masks and objectives. This bootstrapped data pipeline and multi-objective architecture jointly improve alignment, retrieval, captioning, and visual question answering.

records.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models

BLIP-2 keeps both a pre-trained image encoder and a large language model frozen and learns a lightweight Querying Transformer between them. A set of learned query tokens attends to visual features and compresses them into a small representation. The Q-Former is first trained with image-text contrastive, matching, and generation objectives, then connected to the frozen language model through a projection and trained to produce language-compatible visual prompts. This reduces trainable parameters while transferring strong unimodal models into a multimodal system.

records.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Visual Instruction Tuning

LLaVA connects a frozen visual encoder to a large language model with a learned linear projection that maps image features into the language model's token embedding space. Image tokens and text instruction tokens are concatenated and processed autoregressively by the language model. Training proceeds with feature alignment on image-caption pairs followed by visual instruction tuning on multimodal conversations generated from image annotations. The method relies on a simple connector and language-model supervision rather than a large custom multimodal fusion network.

records.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

CLIP trains separate image and text encoders on large batches of paired images and natural-language captions. Each image and text is mapped to a normalized embedding, and a symmetric contrastive loss increases similarity for matched pairs while decreasing similarity for all mismatched pairs in the batch. At inference, class names are converted into textual prompts and embedded by the text encoder, enabling zero-shot classification through image-text similarity. The architecture learns transferable visual concepts directly from language supervision.

records.title: Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Scaling Up Visual and Vision-Language Representation Learning With Noisy Text Supervision

ALIGN uses a dual-encoder contrastive architecture similar to image-text retrieval systems but trains at very large scale on weakly filtered web image and alt-text pairs. An EfficientNet image encoder and a BERT-style text encoder independently produce normalized embeddings. In-batch negatives define a bidirectional contrastive objective that aligns corresponding image and text representations. Rather than relying on expensive curated captions, the methodology emphasizes scale and simple noise filtering to learn a shared cross-modal embedding space.

records.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

SigLIP keeps separate image and text encoders but replaces the global softmax contrastive objective with independent sigmoid binary classification losses for every image-text pair in the batch. Positive pairs are encouraged to have high similarity and negative pairs low similarity, without requiring normalization across the full batch. This removes the need for global all-gather operations used by softmax contrastive learning and makes large distributed training easier to scale while preserving a CLIP-like shared embedding space.

records.title: FILIP: Fine-grained Interactive Language-Image Pre-Training
records.methodology_paraphrase:
FILIP: Fine-grained Interactive Language-Image Pre-Training

FILIP preserves token-level image and text representations instead of reducing each modality to one global vector before alignment. For each image patch, the method finds its maximum similarity to text tokens, and the reverse direction performs the analogous operation. These fine-grained similarities are aggregated into an image-text score and optimized with a contrastive objective. The resulting late-interaction mechanism encourages local visual regions and words to align directly while remaining efficient enough for large-scale dual-encoder pre-training.

records.title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation

ALBEF first aligns image and text embeddings with a contrastive objective before applying a multimodal fusion encoder. A vision Transformer and text encoder produce unimodal features, and a cross-modal Transformer then performs image-text matching and masked language modeling. A momentum teacher supplies soft targets for noisy web data, reducing the effect of incorrect captions. This align-before-fuse strategy separates global representation alignment from detailed cross-modal reasoning and uses self-distillation to improve robustness.

records.title: ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ViLBERT: Pretraining Task-Agnostic Visiolinguistic Representations for Vision-and-Language Tasks

ViLBERT uses two parallel Transformer streams: one processes region-level visual features and the other processes text tokens. Co-attentional Transformer layers periodically exchange information between the streams while preserving modality-specific processing. Pre-training combines masked multimodal modeling with image-text alignment objectives on paired data. The resulting dual-stream representation can be fine-tuned for visual question answering, referring expression tasks, retrieval, and other multimodal problems without redesigning the fusion architecture.

records.title: LXMERT: Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
LXMERT: Learning Cross-Modality Encoder Representations from Transformers

LXMERT separates processing into three encoders. An object-relation encoder models region features from an object detector, a language encoder models word tokens, and a cross-modality encoder applies bidirectional cross-attention to fuse the two streams. Pre-training uses masked language modeling, masked object prediction, cross-modal matching, and visual question answering objectives. This staged architecture allows each modality to develop specialized representations before repeated cross-attention learns detailed visual-language correspondences.

records.title: UNITER: UNiversal Image-TExt Representation Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
UNITER: UNiversal Image-TExt Representation Learning

UNITER uses a single Transformer to jointly encode text tokens and detected image-region features after projecting both into a shared hidden space. Pre-training is performed with several objectives, including masked language modeling, masked region modeling, image-text matching, and word-region alignment based on optimal transport. Hard negative mining strengthens the matching objective. By fusing both modalities from the first Transformer layer, the model learns a unified contextual representation for multimodal understanding tasks.

records.title: VisualBERT: A Simple and Performant Baseline for Vision and Language
records.methodology_paraphrase:
VisualBERT: A Simple and Performant Baseline for Vision and Language

VisualBERT extends a BERT-style encoder by appending visual region embeddings to the text-token sequence. Region features are projected to the same hidden dimension and assigned special positional or segment indicators, allowing standard self-attention to mix visual and linguistic information directly. Pre-training uses masked language modeling and image-text relationship prediction on paired image-caption data. The simplicity of the single-stream design demonstrates that a conventional Transformer can jointly contextualize words and visual regions without specialized co-attention modules.

records.title: OSCAR: Object-Semantics Aligned Pre-training for Vision-Language Tasks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
OSCAR: Object-Semantics Aligned Pre-training for Vision-Language Tasks

OSCAR treats detected object tags as explicit anchor points between image regions and natural-language text. The input sequence contains word tokens, object-label tokens, and region embeddings, all processed by a Transformer. Pre-training objectives reconstruct masked tokens and distinguish correct image-text-tag combinations from mismatched ones. Because object labels provide discrete semantic concepts shared by both modalities, they help reduce the gap between continuous region features and language, improving cross-modal alignment.

records.title: CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
CoCa: Contrastive Captioners are Image-Text Foundation Models

CoCa combines contrastive image-text representation learning and autoregressive captioning in one encoder-decoder architecture. A vision Transformer produces image tokens and a pooled global representation; a text decoder first processes text with causal self-attention and then uses cross-attention to image tokens. The global text and image embeddings optimize a contrastive loss, while the decoder simultaneously predicts caption tokens. This joint objective produces both strong retrieval embeddings and a generative multimodal decoder in a single model.

records.title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners

MAE randomly removes a very large fraction of image patches before encoding. Only the visible patches are processed by a relatively heavy Vision Transformer encoder. A lightweight decoder receives the encoded visible tokens together with learned mask tokens, restores positional order, and reconstructs the pixel values of the missing patches. Because the encoder never processes masked patches, pre-training is computationally efficient. The trained encoder is later transferred to recognition tasks while the reconstruction decoder is discarded.

records.title: BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BEiT: BERT Pre-Training of Image Transformers

BEiT applies masked-token pre-training to images. A discrete visual tokenizer first converts image patches into semantic visual tokens. During pre-training, a subset of image patches is masked, the corrupted patch sequence is processed by a Vision Transformer, and the model predicts the corresponding discrete tokenizer codes at masked positions. The tokenizer is used only to create targets, not as the backbone itself. This formulation adapts BERT-style masked prediction to visual data while preserving a standard Transformer encoder.

records.title: SimMIM: A Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SimMIM: A Simple Framework for Masked Image Modeling

SimMIM masks a large portion of image patches and feeds the corrupted image into a hierarchical or plain vision backbone. A very lightweight prediction head reconstructs raw RGB values for only the masked regions, using a simple regression loss. Unlike approaches that depend on a learned discrete tokenizer or complex decoder, SimMIM keeps both the target representation and prediction head minimal. The methodology shows that high masking ratios and direct low-level reconstruction can still produce transferable visual representations.

records.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning

MoCo maintains a query encoder trained by gradient descent and a key encoder updated as an exponential moving average of the query encoder. Positive pairs are two augmentations of the same image, while negative keys are stored in a large first-in-first-out queue. The momentum encoder changes slowly, keeping queued representations consistent over time. A contrastive loss pulls each query toward its matching key and pushes it away from the queue, decoupling the number of negatives from the mini-batch size.

records.title: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations
records.methodology_paraphrase:
A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

SimCLR generates two independently augmented views of every image, encodes them with a shared backbone, and maps features through a small nonlinear projection head. The NT-Xent contrastive loss treats the paired view as positive and all other views in the batch as negatives, maximizing agreement between matched examples after normalization. Strong stochastic augmentation, large batches, and a projection head are central components. After pre-training, the projection head is discarded and the encoder representation is used for downstream tasks.

records.title: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Bootstrap Your Own Latent: A New Approach to Self-Supervised Learning

BYOL trains an online network to predict the representation produced by a target network for another augmented view of the same image. The target parameters are an exponential moving average of the online parameters and receive no direct gradient. The online branch contains an additional predictor, and the loss minimizes the distance between normalized online predictions and target projections. Because no explicit negative examples are used, the method relies on asymmetric architecture and slow target updates to avoid representational collapse.

records.title: Unsupervised Learning of Visual Features by Contrasting Cluster Assignments
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Unsupervised Learning of Visual Features by Contrasting Cluster Assignments

SwAV learns online prototype vectors and assigns image-view embeddings to these prototypes rather than contrasting every pair of individual examples. Multiple augmented crops of the same image are processed, and the model predicts the cluster assignment of one view from the representation of another. A balanced assignment is obtained with an optimal-transport-style Sinkhorn procedure. Multi-crop augmentation provides many low-resolution views at limited cost, and swapped assignment prediction encourages view-invariant semantic features without maintaining a large memory bank.

records.title: Barlow Twins: Self-Supervised Learning via Redundancy Reduction

records.title: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:

An invariance term makes paired embeddings similar, a variance term forces each feature dimension to maintain a minimum standard deviation and thereby prevents collapse, and a covariance term penalizes off-diagonal correlations across dimensions. records.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

records.title: iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer
records.methodology_paraphrase:

Teacher patch representations act as an online tokenizer target, so the model predicts semantic patch codes without relying on a separately trained discrete tokenizer. records.title: data2vec: A General Framework for Self-supervised Learning in Speech, Vision and Language

Instead of predicting raw pixels, tokens, or hand-designed discrete targets, the student regresses to a contextual target formed by averaging representations from several upper teacher layers. records.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations

A convolutional feature encoder converts raw waveform into latent speech representations. A Transformer context network processes the sequence after contiguous spans have been masked. At masked time steps, a contrastive objective requires the contextual representation to identify the correct quantized target among distractors, while a diversity loss encourages broad codebook usage. records.title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
records.methodology_paraphrase:
HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units

A Transformer then receives waveform-derived features with masked intervals and predicts the cluster identity of masked frames using surrounding context. After learning stronger representations, the hidden features can be reclustered to generate improved targets for another training iteration. The method avoids requiring exact phonetic labels while encouraging the model to capture linguistic structure.

records.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision

Whisper is an encoder-decoder Transformer trained on a very large collection of weakly labeled speech. Multiple speech-processing tasks are therefore expressed through one token prediction objective. records.title: Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Semi-Supervised Classification with Graph Convolutional Networks

Multiplying by the symmetric normalization of this augmented adjacency performs degree-corrected neighborhood averaging, after which a learned weight matrix and nonlinearity are applied. Stacking a small number of such layers propagates label and feature information across the graph. The model is trained with supervised loss only on labeled nodes while leveraging the full graph structure.

records.title: Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Inductive Representation Learning on Large Graphs

GraphSAGE computes node embeddings by repeatedly sampling a fixed-size set of neighbors and aggregating their current representations. At each layer, the aggregated neighborhood vector is combined with the node's own representation and passed through a learned transformation. Mean, LSTM, and pooling aggregators are studied. Because the model learns aggregation functions rather than a separate embedding for every training node, it can generate representations for previously unseen nodes and scale to large graphs through neighborhood sampling.

records.title: Graph Attention Networks

Graph Attention Networks

Each node feature is first linearly transformed; for every connected pair, a shared attention function computes an unnormalized compatibility score that is normalized across the node's neighbors. The output is a weighted sum of transformed neighboring features. Multiple attention heads are used in parallel and are concatenated or averaged. This lets the model learn which neighbors are most informative without requiring fixed degree-based normalization.

records.title: How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?

GIN is designed to match the discriminative power of the Weisfeiler-Lehman graph isomorphism test under neighborhood aggregation. Each layer sums the feature vectors of neighboring nodes and adds a weighted version of the node's own representation. A multi-layer perceptron then applies an injective transformation to the aggregated vector. Graph-level representations are obtained by pooling node embeddings from one or multiple layers. The use of summation and expressive MLPs is central to preserving distinctions between different neighborhood multisets.

records.title: Neural Message Passing for Quantum Chemistry

For each edge, a learned message function combines the states of the incident nodes with edge attributes. Messages arriving at a node are aggregated and used by an update function to produce the next node state. After several iterations, a permutation-invariant readout maps the set of node states to a graph-level prediction. records.title: Gated Graph Sequence Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Gated Graph Sequence Neural Networks

GGNN performs recurrent message passing over a graph. At each propagation step, every node receives a sum of linear transformations of neighboring hidden states, with transformation parameters depending on edge type. A GRU-style gated update then combines the aggregated message with the node's previous hidden state. Repeating this procedure lets information travel through multiple graph hops while preserving recurrent memory. Task-specific output modules use the final node states for graph annotation or sequential prediction problems.

records.title: Residual Gated Graph ConvNets
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Residual Gated Graph ConvNets

Node and edge representations are updated together inside residual blocks. Edge features are transformed into sigmoid gates, normalized across the neighborhood, and used to weight incoming node messages; node updates then combine these gated messages with the previous node state. Residual connections and normalization make deeper graph networks trainable while retaining explicit edge-conditioned communication.

records.title: Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Principal Neighbourhood Aggregation for Graph Nets

PNA uses multiple neighborhood aggregators in parallel rather than relying on a single sum or mean. Statistics such as mean, maximum, minimum, and standard deviation capture complementary aspects of a node's neighbor distribution. Degree-dependent scalers then amplify or attenuate the aggregated features based on how a node's degree compares with the training distribution. Concatenating these transformed statistics before an MLP gives the network a richer, degree-aware summary of local graph structure.

records.title: Simple and Deep Graph Convolutional Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Simple and Deep Graph Convolutional Networks

GCNII modifies graph convolution to support much greater depth. Each layer includes an initial residual connection that injects a controlled fraction of the original node features, preventing representations from drifting entirely toward over-smoothed neighborhood averages. An identity mapping term blends the learned transformation with the identity matrix, with layer-dependent strength. These mechanisms preserve discriminative information and stabilize optimization as many graph propagation layers are stacked, allowing deeper receptive fields than conventional GCNs.

records.title: Predict then Propagate: Graph Neural Networks meet Personalized PageRank
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Predict then Propagate: Graph Neural Networks meet Personalized PageRank

These outputs are then repeatedly propagated with a personalized PageRank update that mixes iterative neighborhood propagation with a fixed teleport probability back to the initial prediction. Because the propagation parameters are not learned layer by layer, the method can use many graph propagation steps without the same parameter growth or overfitting as deep GCN stacks.

records.title: SIGN: Scalable Inception Graph Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SIGN: Scalable Inception Graph Neural Networks

SIGN precomputes several graph-propagated versions of the input features using different adjacency-derived operators or hop distances. During training, these cached feature matrices are independently transformed by small MLP branches and concatenated before a final classifier. Since neighborhood aggregation is completed before optimization, mini-batches no longer require recursive neighbor sampling or message passing. The model resembles an Inception module over multiple graph receptive fields and is designed for high-throughput training on very large graphs.

records.title: Graph U-Nets
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Graph U-Nets

Graph U-Net introduces learnable pooling and unpooling for graph-structured data. A graph pooling layer scores nodes with a trainable projection, retains the top-scoring subset, and gates the selected node features while inducing a smaller adjacency structure. Graph convolution operates on the coarsened graph. The decoder later restores nodes to their original positions through unpooling and combines features with encoder skip connections. This creates a hierarchical encoder-decoder graph architecture analogous to U-Net on regular grids.

records.title: Dynamic Graph CNN for Learning on Point Clouds
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Dynamic Graph CNN for Learning on Point Clouds

DGCNN repeatedly constructs a k-nearest-neighbor graph in the current feature space rather than using a fixed graph. Its EdgeConv operator builds edge features from a node representation together with the difference between that node and each neighbor, applies a shared MLP, and aggregates neighbor edge features with a symmetric max operation. Recomputing neighborhoods after each layer lets graph connectivity evolve with learned semantics, enabling the model to capture local geometric relations in point clouds.

records.title: Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?

Do Transformers Really Perform Bad for Graph Representation?

Shortest-path distance between nodes is encoded as a spatial attention bias, edge features along the connecting path contribute additional bias terms, and node centrality is represented through degree embeddings. With these graph-aware encodings, full self-attention can operate over all node pairs while still distinguishing graph topology. A virtual graph token can aggregate global information for graph-level prediction tasks.

records.title: Recipe for a General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:

The local branch uses an established graph neural operator to capture edge-based inductive bias, while the global branch performs Transformer-style interaction among nodes using full or scalable attention. Positional and structural encodings supply graph geometry or topology information. The two branch outputs are fused with residual and feed-forward components, providing a modular recipe that balances local graph structure with long-range global communication.

records.title: SchNet: A Continuous-filter Convolutional Neural Network for Modeling Quantum Interactions
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SchNet: A Continuous-filter Convolutional Neural Network for Modeling Quantum Interactions

SchNet represents atoms with learned embeddings and repeatedly applies interaction blocks based on pairwise distances. Distances are expanded with radial basis functions and passed through a small network to generate continuous convolution filters. Each atom receives a weighted sum of neighboring atom features using these distance-conditioned filters, followed by atom-wise transformations and residual updates. Because the filters depend only on interatomic distance, the representation is invariant to global translation and rotation while remaining sensitive to molecular geometry.

records.title: Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs

Directional Message Passing for Molecular Graphs

DimeNet augments molecular message passing with explicit angular information. Radial basis functions encode pairwise distances, while spherical basis functions encode the angle formed by triplets of atoms. Messages are associated with directed edges and updated using neighboring directed edges together with their distance and angle embeddings. This directional interaction captures bond geometry beyond simple pairwise distance. Learned output blocks aggregate edge representations into atom-wise contributions that are summed to predict molecular properties.

records.title: Fast and Uncertainty-Aware Directional Message Passing for Non-Equilibrium Molecules
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Fast and Uncertainty-Aware Directional Message Passing for Non-Equilibrium Molecules

DimeNet++ keeps the directional distance-and-angle message-passing principle of DimeNet but reorganizes the network for much greater computational efficiency. Embedding sizes and block structure are reduced, separate bilinear interaction layers are simplified, and residual MLP components are redesigned while retaining radial and spherical basis encodings. Directed edge messages still exchange information through atom triplets, preserving geometric expressiveness but with lower memory use and faster training and inference.

records.title: Equivariant Message Passing for the Prediction of Tensorial Properties and Molecular Spectra
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Equivariant Message Passing for the Prediction of Tensorial Properties and Molecular Spectra

PaiNN maintains both scalar node features and three-dimensional vector features. Messages are functions of interatomic distances and neighboring scalar/vector states, and updates mix scalar and vector channels through operations that preserve rotational equivariance. Vector features rotate with the molecular geometry, while scalar outputs remain invariant when required. Repeated message and update blocks therefore capture directional interactions without choosing a fixed coordinate frame, enabling prediction of energies, forces, dipoles, and other tensorial molecular properties.

records.title: GemNet: Universal Directional Graph Neural Networks for Molecules
records.methodology_paraphrase:
GemNet: Universal Directional Graph Neural Networks for Molecules

GemNet extends directional molecular message passing by using edge embeddings, triplet interactions, and higher-order geometric relationships while preserving invariance to rigid transformations. Radial basis functions encode distances and spherical basis functions encode directional angles. Messages are propagated along directed edges and enriched with information from neighboring edge configurations, then aggregated into atom representations and graph-level predictions. The architecture is designed to increase geometric expressiveness while keeping the interaction blocks structured and physically consistent.

records.title: E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials
records.methodology_paraphrase:
E(3)-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Data-Efficient and Accurate Interatomic Potentials

NequIP represents atomic features as irreducible representations of the three-dimensional rotation group. Neighbor information is combined using tensor products between learned features and spherical harmonics of relative atomic directions, with radial neural networks controlling distance-dependent weights. Equivariant nonlinearities and gated updates preserve the transformation rules of each feature type across layers. Scalar energy contributions are predicted invariantly, while forces are obtained through energy gradients, giving a data-efficient equivariant interatomic potential.

records.title: E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks

EGNN jointly updates node features and coordinates while guaranteeing equivariance to translations, rotations, reflections, and permutations. Edge messages depend on node attributes and squared pairwise distances, which are invariant to rigid transformations. Coordinate updates are expressed as weighted sums of relative displacement vectors, so they transform consistently when the whole system is rotated or translated. This avoids spherical harmonics and tensor products while still allowing geometry to evolve inside the network.

records.title: SE(3)-Transformers: 3D Roto-Translation Equivariant Attention Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SE(3)-Transformers: 3D Roto-Translation Equivariant Attention Networks

SE(3)-Transformer generalizes self-attention to three-dimensional equivariant features. Queries, keys, and values are organized into representation types that transform according to irreducible representations of SO(3). Attention weights are invariant scalars, while value transformations use spherical harmonics and tensor-product kernels so the output transforms predictably under rotations and translations. The architecture combines graph attention with equivariant convolutional structure, enabling long-range interaction among points while respecting 3D geometry.

records.title: Tensor Field Networks: Rotation- and Translation-Equivariant Neural Networks for 3D Point Clouds
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Tensor Field Networks: Rotation- and Translation-Equivariant Neural Networks for 3D Point Clouds

Tensor Field Networks represent each point with features transforming as scalars, vectors, or higher-order tensors. Convolution kernels are constructed from learnable radial functions multiplied by spherical harmonics, and tensor products combine input feature types with kernel types according to rotation-group rules. Summing these equivariant messages over neighbors preserves translation and rotation behavior exactly. Stacking such layers yields a neural field whose intermediate and output tensors transform consistently with the underlying 3D point cloud.

records.title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation

PointNet processes each point independently with a shared MLP and then aggregates all point features using a symmetric max-pooling operation, ensuring invariance to point ordering. Learned transformation networks can predict affine alignment matrices for input coordinates and intermediate features. The pooled global vector is used directly for classification or concatenated back to per-point features for segmentation. The architecture deliberately avoids voxelization or graph construction and treats the point cloud as an unordered set.

records.title: PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space

PointNet++ builds a hierarchy over point sets. Farthest-point sampling selects local region centers, neighborhood queries collect nearby points at one or more radii, and a PointNet-style shared MLP plus symmetric pooling summarizes each local set. Repeating sampling and grouping at coarser scales progressively enlarges the receptive field. Feature-propagation layers interpolate coarse features back to denser points for segmentation. The hierarchy allows the model to capture local geometric structure that a single global PointNet pooling operation cannot represent.

records.title: Point Transformer
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Point Transformer

Point Transformer defines a local self-attention operator directly on point clouds. For each point, neighboring points are selected and their features are linearly projected. Relative 3D coordinates are passed through an MLP to produce positional encodings that influence both attention weights and value features. Vector-valued attention weights modulate neighbor contributions before aggregation. The operator is embedded in residual blocks and hierarchical sampling stages, combining permutation invariance with geometry-aware local attention for point classification and dense prediction.

records.title: PointNeXt: Revisiting PointNet++ with Improved Training and Scaling Strategies
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PointNeXt: Revisiting PointNet++ with Improved Training and Scaling Strategies

PointNeXt retains the simple set-abstraction hierarchy of PointNet++ but modernizes the residual block, scaling strategy, and training recipe. Local neighborhoods are grouped around sampled centers, transformed with shared MLPs, and pooled, while inverted residual-style channel expansion improves capacity. Stage depths and widths are scaled systematically, and augmentation, optimization, and regularization are strengthened. The work shows that a carefully scaled and trained PointNet++ family can remain highly competitive without introducing substantially more complex point operators.

records.title: Point-BERT: Pre-training 3D Point Cloud Transformers with Masked Point Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Point-BERT: Pre-training 3D Point Cloud Transformers with Masked Point Modeling

Point-BERT first divides a point cloud into local patches and converts each patch into a discrete token using a learned tokenizer. A Transformer receives visible patch embeddings while a subset of patch tokens is masked, and it predicts the corresponding discrete visual vocabulary entries. Positional embeddings are derived from patch centers. The masked-token pre-training objective encourages contextual 3D reasoning, after which the Transformer is fine-tuned for classification and segmentation using continuous patch features rather than relying solely on the tokenizer.

records.title: Masked Autoencoders for Point Cloud Self-supervised Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Masked Autoencoders for Point Cloud Self-supervised Learning

Point-MAE partitions a point cloud into local groups, randomly masks most groups, and encodes only the visible groups with a Transformer. A lightweight decoder receives encoded visible tokens together with mask tokens and reconstructs the coordinates of the missing local patches. Positional information comes from group centers, and the reconstruction loss is typically based on point-set distance. By excluding masked groups from the encoder, the method learns efficient contextual representations while avoiding the need for discrete point tokenizers.

records.title: PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PointPillars: Fast Encoders for Object Detection from Point Clouds

PointPillars partitions the ground plane into vertical columns called pillars without discretizing the vertical dimension. Points inside each pillar are augmented with offsets to the pillar mean and center, transformed independently by a small PointNet, and max-pooled into a fixed pillar feature. These features are scattered into a pseudo-image on the BEV grid, after which a conventional 2D convolutional backbone and detection head predict oriented 3D boxes. The design converts sparse point clouds into an efficient dense 2D representation.

records.title: VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
VoxelNet: End-to-End Learning for Point Cloud Based 3D Object Detection

VoxelNet divides a point cloud into equally spaced 3D voxels. Within each non-empty voxel, a Voxel Feature Encoding layer applies point-wise transformations, aggregates a local max feature, and concatenates the result back to each point to learn interactions among points in the same voxel. Stacked VFE layers produce one feature per voxel. Sparse 3D convolutional middle layers then aggregate spatial context before a region-proposal-style network predicts oriented 3D bounding boxes.

records.title: SECOND: Sparsely Embedded Convolutional Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
SECOND: Sparsely Embedded Convolutional Detection

SECOND builds on voxelized point-cloud detection but replaces dense 3D convolution with sparse convolution that operates only at occupied voxel locations. Points are encoded into voxel features, sparse 3D convolutional blocks aggregate local geometric context, and the representation is collapsed into a bird's-eye-view feature map. A one-stage detection head predicts class scores and box offsets from anchors. The sparse computation substantially reduces the cost of high-resolution 3D feature extraction without discarding the voxel structure.

records.title: Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Center-based 3D Object Detection and Tracking

CenterPoint represents each 3D object by the center of its bounding box on a bird's-eye-view feature map. A voxel- or pillar-based backbone produces BEV features, and a keypoint-style head predicts a heatmap of object centers together with offsets, height, dimensions, and orientation. Candidate centers are decoded directly rather than matched to dense anchors. A second-stage refinement module can pool point or BEV features around predicted boxes, and the same center representation supports simple tracking by associating motion-adjusted detections.

records.title: BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BEVFormer: Learning Bird's-Eye-View Representation from Multi-Camera Images via Spatiotemporal Transformers

Spatial cross-attention projects reference points from each BEV query into multiple camera views and samples corresponding image features using deformable attention. Temporal self-attention aligns the current BEV grid with the previous frame using ego-motion and combines historical information. Stacked encoder layers update the BEV representation, which is then consumed by 3D detection or map heads. The architecture constructs a unified spatial feature map without explicit depth prediction.

records.title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation

BEVFusion converts camera and LiDAR information into a common bird's-eye-view feature space before fusion. Image features are lifted and transformed into BEV using geometric projection, while LiDAR features are produced by a voxelized or pillar-based 3D backbone and collapsed into the same grid. Modality-specific BEV tensors are concatenated or fused with convolution, and shared task heads operate on the resulting representation. This separates sensor encoding from downstream perception and supports detection and segmentation with a common fused backbone.

records.title: PETR: Position Embedding Transformation for Multi-View 3D Object Detection
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PETR: Position Embedding Transformation for Multi-View 3D Object Detection

PETR transforms 3D coordinates sampled along camera rays into positional embeddings that are added to multi-view image features. A set of learned 3D object queries is processed by a Transformer decoder, whose cross-attention operates on image features enriched with these 3D-aware positional encodings. Each query predicts a class and 3D bounding box. Rather than explicitly generating depth maps or BEV features, PETR lets the decoder reason about spatial location through the transformed position representation attached to perspective-view features.

records.title: DETR3D: 3D Object Detection from Multi-view Images via 3D-to-2D Queries
records.methodology_paraphrase:
DETR3D: 3D Object Detection from Multi-view Images via 3D-to-2D Queries

DETR3D represents each object query with a learned feature and a 3D reference point. The reference point is projected through known camera calibration matrices into all image views, and multi-scale image features are sampled around the projected locations. The sampled features are aggregated to update the query through a Transformer decoder, which iteratively refines 3D boxes and class scores. This query-centric 3D-to-2D sampling avoids constructing a dense voxel or BEV volume from camera features.

records.title: TransFusion: Robust LiDAR-Camera Fusion for 3D Object Detection with Transformers
records.methodology_paraphrase:
TransFusion: Robust LiDAR-Camera Fusion for 3D Object Detection with Transformers

TransFusion first generates object proposals from LiDAR BEV features and represents them as Transformer queries. Cross-attention then associates each proposal with relevant image features rather than fusing modalities densely everywhere. The decoder refines object representations using both LiDAR geometry and camera appearance, followed by class and box prediction. The method also uses category-aware query initialization and image-guided feature aggregation so that camera information improves semantic recognition while LiDAR remains the primary geometric reference.

records.title: 4D Spatio-Temporal ConvNets: Minkowski Convolutional Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
4D Spatio-Temporal ConvNets: Minkowski Convolutional Neural Networks

Minkowski convolution generalizes sparse convolution to arbitrary-dimensional sparse coordinates. Features are stored only at occupied lattice locations, and convolution gathers neighboring active coordinates according to a kernel offset set. Hash-based coordinate management tracks sparse input-output mappings efficiently as resolution changes. Residual sparse convolution blocks can therefore be assembled into U-Net or ResNet-style architectures over 3D or 4D point data, allowing spatial and spatiotemporal processing without allocating dense voxel tensors.

records.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes

A variational autoencoder introduces a latent variable model with an encoder that predicts the parameters of an approximate posterior distribution over latent codes and a decoder that defines the likelihood of the observation given a latent sample. The reparameterization trick expresses sampling as a differentiable transformation of noise, allowing gradient-based optimization. Training maximizes the evidence lower bound, combining reconstruction likelihood with a KL divergence that regularizes the approximate posterior toward a prior. New samples are generated by decoding latent draws from the prior.

records.title: beta-VAE: Learning Basic Visual Concepts with a Constrained Variational Framework
records.methodology_paraphrase:
beta-VAE: Learning Basic Visual Concepts with a Constrained Variational Framework
