The encoder and decoder retain the same probabilistic structure, but the stronger pressure toward the factorized prior restricts latent capacity and encourages statistically more independent latent dimensions. Reconstruction quality and latent compression are therefore traded against disentanglement. The model is trained entirely from observations without supervision about the underlying generative factors, and latent dimensions can emerge that correspond to interpretable data variations.

records.title: Neural Discrete Representation Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Neural Discrete Representation Learning

VQ-VAE replaces the continuous latent distribution of a standard VAE with a finite codebook of embedding vectors. The encoder produces continuous features that are quantized to the nearest codebook entries before being passed to the decoder. A straight-through estimator carries reconstruction gradients to the encoder, while codebook and commitment losses align encoder outputs with selected embeddings. After the autoencoder is trained, a separate autoregressive prior can model the discrete latent sequence, enabling high-level generation in a compact token space.

records.title: Generating Diverse High-Fidelity Images with VQ-VAE-2
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Generating Diverse High-Fidelity Images with VQ-VAE-2

VQ-VAE-2 extends vector-quantized autoencoding to a hierarchy of discrete latent maps. A top latent grid captures global structure, while a lower latent grid encodes finer details conditioned on the top representation. Each level uses nearest-neighbor codebook quantization and a convolutional decoder reconstructs the image from both. After learning the autoencoder, powerful autoregressive priors are trained over the top and bottom discrete codes. Generation samples global codes first and then conditioned fine-scale codes before decoding.

records.title: Wasserstein Auto-Encoders
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Wasserstein Auto-Encoders

Wasserstein Auto-Encoders train an encoder-decoder pair by minimizing reconstruction cost while matching the aggregated distribution of encoded data to a chosen latent prior. Unlike a VAE, regularization is applied to the marginal code distribution rather than to each individual approximate posterior. The distribution match can be enforced through a GAN-style discriminator or a kernel-based maximum mean discrepancy penalty. This objective arises from an optimal-transport formulation and supports deterministic as well as stochastic encoders.

records.title: Adversarial Autoencoders
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Adversarial Autoencoders

An adversarial autoencoder combines a reconstruction autoencoder with adversarial regularization in latent space. The encoder maps data to latent codes and the decoder reconstructs the inputs. A discriminator is trained to distinguish encoded samples from samples drawn from a desired prior, while the encoder is trained to fool the discriminator. Alternating reconstruction and adversarial phases forces the aggregated latent distribution toward the prior. By choosing structured priors, the method can support clustering, semi-supervised learning, or controllable latent factors.

records.title: Generative Adversarial Nets
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Generative Adversarial Nets

A generator transforms random noise into synthetic samples, while a discriminator receives both real data and generated samples and predicts their source. Training is formulated as a two-player minimax game: the discriminator improves its ability to separate real from fake, and the generator updates its parameters to make generated samples increasingly difficult to distinguish from real observations. In the idealized equilibrium, the generator distribution matches the data distribution. Sampling requires only a forward pass through the trained generator, without explicit likelihood evaluation.

records.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks

DCGAN adapts adversarial generation to images using a set of architectural constraints. The generator uses learned convolutional upsampling from a low-dimensional noise vector, while the discriminator uses strided convolutions for downsampling; pooling and large fully connected stacks are avoided. Batch normalization stabilizes most layers, ReLU is used in the generator, and leaky ReLU in the discriminator. The convolutional hierarchy encourages spatially coherent image synthesis and also yields discriminator features useful for unsupervised representation learning.

records.title: Wasserstein GAN
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Wasserstein GAN

WGAN replaces the original adversarial divergence with the Earth-Mover or Wasserstein-1 distance. The discriminator becomes a critic that outputs unrestricted real-valued scores rather than probabilities. Training alternates several critic updates with generator updates, and the critic is constrained to be Lipschitz by clipping its parameters to a fixed range. The generator minimizes the negative critic score of generated samples. This objective provides a smoother learning signal and a critic loss that correlates more meaningfully with sample quality than the original GAN loss.

records.title: Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Improved Training of Wasserstein GANs

WGAN-GP enforces the Lipschitz constraint through a gradient penalty instead of weight clipping. The critic is evaluated at random points interpolated between real and generated samples, and an auxiliary loss penalizes deviations of the gradient norm with respect to those inputs from one. The critic still optimizes the Wasserstein score difference and the generator maximizes the critic's score on synthetic samples. The gradient constraint stabilizes training while allowing the critic to use its full parameter range.

records.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks

StyleGAN maps the input noise vector through an MLP into an intermediate latent space. Learned affine transformations convert this latent code into per-layer style parameters that modulate feature statistics through adaptive instance normalization. The synthesis network begins from a learned constant rather than directly from the noise vector, and independent stochastic noise is injected at each resolution to control fine detail. Styles can be mixed across layers, separating coarse attributes from high-frequency stochastic variation and producing a more disentangled control space.

records.title: Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Analyzing and Improving the Image Quality of StyleGAN

StyleGAN2 replaces adaptive instance normalization with weight modulation and demodulation. Each convolutional kernel is scaled by style coefficients derived from the latent code, then normalized to prevent style-dependent signal amplification. This removes characteristic artifacts caused by normalization inside the original generator. The architecture also revises progressive growing, introduces path-length regularization to encourage predictable latent-to-image changes, and adjusts discriminator regularization. The resulting synthesis network maintains layer-wise style control while improving image fidelity and stability.

records.title: Alias-Free Generative Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Alias-Free Generative Adversarial Networks

StyleGAN3 redesigns the generator so that image features behave consistently under continuous translation and, in one variant, rotation. The network treats feature maps as samples of continuous signals and uses carefully designed low-pass filters around upsampling, nonlinearities, and resampling operations to suppress aliasing. Positional information from fixed pixel coordinates is removed where possible. Style modulation remains, but the synthesis pipeline becomes approximately equivariant to geometric transformations, reducing texture sticking and improving the physical consistency of generated motion.

records.title: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis

BigGAN scales class-conditional adversarial training through much larger batch sizes, wider networks, and large embedding dimensions. The generator uses residual upsampling blocks and conditions batch-normalization parameters on class embeddings, while the discriminator uses residual downsampling blocks and projection-based class conditioning. Spectral normalization stabilizes both networks. Orthogonal regularization and a truncation strategy at sampling time control the trade-off between diversity and fidelity. The method demonstrates that aggressive scale and conditioning can substantially improve high-resolution synthesis.

records.title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation using Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks

CycleGAN learns two mappings between image domains using unpaired datasets. Each direction has its own generator and discriminator, with adversarial losses encouraging translated images to resemble the target domain. A cycle-consistency loss requires that translating an image to the other domain and back reconstructs the original input, preventing arbitrary mappings that satisfy only the discriminators. An optional identity loss discourages unnecessary changes when an image is already from the target domain. No paired correspondence between training images is required.

records.title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks

Pix2Pix trains a conditional generator and discriminator from aligned input-output image pairs. The generator uses an encoder-decoder with skip connections so low-level spatial information can pass directly from encoder layers to corresponding decoder layers. The discriminator is a PatchGAN that classifies overlapping local image patches as real or fake, encouraging high-frequency realism. Training combines the adversarial objective with an L1 reconstruction loss between generated and ground-truth targets, balancing realistic texture with global structural fidelity to the conditioning image.

records.title: StarGAN: Unified Generative Adversarial Networks for Multi-Domain Image-to-Image Translation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
StarGAN: Unified Generative Adversarial Networks for Multi-Domain Image-to-Image Translation

StarGAN uses one generator to translate an input image into any of several target domains specified by a domain label. The discriminator performs two tasks: distinguishing real from generated images and predicting the domain label of real images. The generator is trained with adversarial loss, target-domain classification loss, and a reconstruction loss that recovers the original image when the generated sample is translated back to the source domain. This shares parameters across all translation directions instead of training a separate model for each domain pair.

records.title: Semantic Image Synthesis with Spatially-Adaptive Normalization
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Semantic Image Synthesis with Spatially-Adaptive Normalization

SPADE conditions image generation on a semantic segmentation map through spatially adaptive normalization. In each generator block, activations are normalized channel-wise, but the scale and bias parameters are predicted as spatial maps from the resized segmentation layout. This prevents semantic information from being washed away by conventional normalization layers. A residual generator progressively upsamples features while repeatedly injecting the semantic map through SPADE layers, allowing object identity and boundary structure to remain aligned with the conditioning layout.

records.title: Photo-Realistic Single Image Super-Resolution Using a Generative Adversarial Network
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Photo-Realistic Single Image Super-Resolution Using a Generative Adversarial Network

SRGAN uses a deep residual generator to upsample a low-resolution image and a discriminator to distinguish reconstructed images from real high-resolution images. The generator contains residual convolutional blocks followed by learned sub-pixel upsampling. Instead of optimizing only pixel-wise error, training combines adversarial loss with a perceptual content loss computed from high-level features of a pre-trained classification network. This encourages reconstructions with visually plausible textures and perceptual detail rather than overly smooth averages.

records.title: ESRGAN: Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
ESRGAN: Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks

ESRGAN strengthens SRGAN with Residual-in-Residual Dense Blocks that remove batch normalization and combine dense connectivity with nested residual scaling. The discriminator uses a relativistic objective that estimates whether a real image looks more realistic than a generated image rather than judging each independently. Perceptual loss is computed from features before activation in a pre-trained network to preserve brightness and texture information. These changes improve high-frequency detail while stabilizing the deep super-resolution generator.

records.title: Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data

Real-ESRGAN trains super-resolution models on synthetic low-resolution images produced by a high-order degradation pipeline. Multiple blur, resize, noise, compression, and ringing operations are applied in randomized sequences to better approximate unknown real-world corruption. The generator builds on ESRGAN-style residual dense blocks, while a U-Net discriminator with spectral normalization provides spatially detailed adversarial feedback. A sharpened ground-truth strategy and realistic degradation synthesis allow the model to handle images without paired real low/high-resolution training data.

records.title: Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Conditional Image Generation with PixelCNN Decoders

PixelCNN factorizes an image distribution autoregressively over pixels. Masked convolutions ensure that the prediction for each pixel depends only on previously generated pixels according to a fixed raster ordering. Gated convolutional blocks increase nonlinear capacity while preserving the causality mask, and class or latent conditioning can be injected into the gates. During training all pixel conditionals are evaluated in parallel because the target image is known, while sampling proceeds sequentially by repeatedly drawing the next pixel from its predicted distribution.

records.title: Pixel Recurrent Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Pixel Recurrent Neural Networks

PixelRNN models images one pixel at a time using two-dimensional recurrent structures that preserve a raster-scan dependency order. Row LSTM and Diagonal BiLSTM variants propagate hidden information across spatial positions while masked input-to-state operations prevent access to future pixels. The model outputs a conditional distribution over each pixel's color channels given all previously generated pixels. Residual and skip connections support deep recurrent stacks. Exact log-likelihood training is possible because the joint image probability is explicitly factorized.

records.title: PixelSNAIL: An Improved Autoregressive Generative Model
records.methodology_paraphrase:
PixelSNAIL: An Improved Autoregressive Generative Model

PixelSNAIL combines masked convolutional residual blocks with causal self-attention. Convolutions efficiently capture local spatial structure, while attention allows each pixel to directly reference distant previously generated pixels under an autoregressive mask. Gated residual units, positional information, and skip connections are used throughout the network. The output parameterizes the conditional distribution of each pixel or discrete latent token. This hybrid improves long-range coherence while retaining exact likelihood training and sequential autoregressive sampling.

records.title: Glow: Generative Flow with Invertible 1x1 Convolutions
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Glow: Generative Flow with Invertible 1x1 Convolutions

Glow builds an exact-likelihood generative model from a sequence of invertible transformations. Each flow step applies act normalization, an invertible 1×1 convolution that learns a permutation and mixing of channels, and an affine coupling layer in which one subset of activations predicts scale and shift parameters for the other subset. Multi-scale squeezing and factor-out operations progressively reorganize spatial resolution and latent variables. Because every transformation has a tractable Jacobian determinant, the model supports exact log-likelihood training and exact inversion between images and latent codes.

records.title: Density Estimation using Real NVP
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Density Estimation using Real NVP

RealNVP constructs an invertible mapping between data and a simple latent distribution using affine coupling layers. Each coupling layer leaves one partition of the variables unchanged and uses it to predict scale and translation functions applied to the remaining variables, giving an easily computed triangular Jacobian. Alternating partitions and multi-scale squeezing allow all dimensions to interact across layers. The model is trained by exact maximum likelihood and can generate samples or infer latent representations by running the same network in opposite directions.

records.title: MADE: Masked Autoencoder for Distribution Estimation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
MADE: Masked Autoencoder for Distribution Estimation

MADE turns a feed-forward autoencoder into an autoregressive density estimator by applying binary masks to network connections. The masks enforce an ordering so that the output distribution parameters for variable x_i depend only on variables that appear earlier in the chosen ordering. All conditional distributions can therefore be computed in a single parallel forward pass during training, even though the joint density is autoregressive. Different masks can represent different orderings, and standard backpropagation trains the masked network by maximum likelihood.

records.title: Masked Autoregressive Flow for Density Estimation
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Masked Autoregressive Flow for Density Estimation

MAF stacks invertible autoregressive transformations whose shift and scale parameters are predicted by masked autoregressive networks. For density estimation, a complete data vector can be transformed to the base distribution in parallel because all autoregressive conditionals are computed simultaneously. The triangular Jacobian makes the log-determinant inexpensive. Reversing the transformation requires sequential sampling, which is acceptable when likelihood evaluation is the primary objective. Permutations between flow steps allow different dimensions to condition on one another across the stack.

records.title: Improved Variational Inference with Inverse Autoregressive Flow
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Improved Variational Inference with Inverse Autoregressive Flow

Inverse Autoregressive Flow enriches an approximate posterior by transforming a simple base sample through a sequence of autoregressive affine updates. A masked autoregressive network predicts shift and scale terms from earlier noise variables, but the direction is chosen so that all output dimensions can be generated in parallel from the base noise. The Jacobian remains triangular, so the density correction is tractable. This makes IAF well suited for flexible variational posteriors in latent-variable models while preserving efficient sampling during training.

records.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
records.methodology_paraphrase:
NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis

NeRF represents a static scene with an MLP that maps a 3D position and viewing direction to volume density and emitted color. For each camera ray, points are sampled through the scene, evaluated by the network, and composited with differentiable volume rendering to predict the pixel color. Positional encoding expands coordinates into higher-frequency sinusoidal features so the MLP can represent fine detail. A coarse network first proposes important ray intervals, and a fine network resamples those intervals more densely for hierarchical rendering.

records.title: Instant Neural Graphics Primitives with a Multiresolution Hash Encoding
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Instant Neural Graphics Primitives with a Multiresolution Hash Encoding

Instant-NGP replaces expensive coordinate-network feature computation with a trainable multiresolution hash-grid encoding. A 3D coordinate is interpolated within several grids of increasing resolution, and grid vertices index compact feature tables through spatial hashing. The concatenated multi-scale features are processed by a small MLP for density and color prediction. Fused GPU kernels update the hash tables and network efficiently. This representation concentrates parameters where needed and dramatically accelerates training and rendering of coordinate-based neural graphics primitives.

records.title: Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mip-NeRF: A Multiscale Representation for Anti-Aliasing Neural Radiance Fields

Mip-NeRF models each conical camera ray as a sequence of volumetric frustums rather than infinitesimal points. For every frustum, the positional encoding is analytically integrated over the corresponding 3D Gaussian approximation, producing an integrated positional encoding that represents the region's expected Fourier features. The radiance-field MLP then predicts density and color from these scale-aware features. Volume rendering proceeds as in NeRF. By accounting for the footprint of each pixel, the model reduces aliasing and improves rendering across different viewing resolutions.

records.title: NeRF++: Analyzing and Improving Neural Radiance Fields
records.methodology_paraphrase:
NeRF++: Analyzing and Improving Neural Radiance Fields

NeRF++ separates an unbounded scene into a bounded foreground volume and an external background volume. The foreground is modeled with a conventional radiance field, while background points are parameterized using an inverted-sphere coordinate system that maps locations outside the unit sphere into a bounded domain. Separate neural fields predict density and color for the two regions, and their samples are composited along the same camera ray. This parameterization allows neural volume rendering to represent distant scene content without imposing an arbitrary far plane.

records.title: Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Plenoxels: Radiance Fields without Neural Networks

Plenoxels represents a radiance field explicitly on a sparse 3D voxel grid rather than with an MLP. Each occupied voxel stores density and spherical-harmonic coefficients for view-dependent color. Pixel values are rendered by trilinearly interpolating these parameters at sampled ray locations and applying standard volume compositing. The voxel parameters are optimized directly with gradient descent, while sparsity pruning and regularization control memory and geometry. Removing the coordinate network greatly accelerates optimization and rendering while retaining differentiable radiance-field training.

records.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
records.methodology_paraphrase:
3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering

The scene is represented by a set of anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives, each with a position, covariance, opacity, and view-dependent color coefficients. Gaussians are projected into the image plane and rasterized using differentiable alpha compositing in a visibility-aware order. Training optimizes primitive parameters against multi-view images and periodically densifies or prunes Gaussians based on gradient and visibility statistics. The explicit representation avoids repeated volumetric MLP evaluation and supports high-quality novel-view rendering at real-time frame rates.

records.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms

PPO alternates between collecting trajectories with the current policy and optimizing a surrogate policy-gradient objective over several minibatch epochs. The probability ratio between the new and behavior policies is clipped to a fixed interval, preventing a single update from changing action probabilities too far even when the estimated advantage is large. A value-function loss and entropy bonus are typically optimized jointly. This simple clipped objective approximates trust-region behavior while using standard first-order stochastic gradient methods and straightforward implementation.

records.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor

SAC optimizes a stochastic policy under the maximum-entropy objective, rewarding both expected return and policy entropy. A replay buffer supports off-policy learning. Two soft Q-functions are trained with bootstrapped targets to reduce positive bias, and the actor is updated through a reparameterized action sample to maximize Q value plus entropy. Target Q networks are updated slowly. A temperature parameter controls the entropy-return trade-off and can itself be learned so that policy stochasticity adapts automatically during training.

records.title: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods

TD3 modifies deterministic actor-critic learning with three mechanisms. Two independently parameterized critics are trained, and the smaller target value is used in Bellman backups to reduce overestimation. Target actions are perturbed with clipped noise before evaluating the target critics, smoothing the value estimate over nearby actions. Finally, the actor and target networks are updated less frequently than the critics. These changes stabilize continuous-control learning while retaining an off-policy replay buffer and deterministic policy.

records.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning

DQN approximates the action-value function with a convolutional neural network that receives a stack of recent game frames and outputs a Q value for every discrete action. Training minimizes a temporal-difference error using transitions sampled uniformly from an experience replay buffer, breaking strong temporal correlations in online data. A separate target network supplies relatively stable bootstrap values and is periodically updated from the online network. Action selection follows an epsilon-greedy policy while the Q-network is improved from replayed experience.

records.title: Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Rainbow: Combining Improvements in Deep Reinforcement Learning

Rainbow integrates several complementary DQN extensions into one agent. It combines double Q-learning for reduced overestimation, prioritized experience replay, dueling value and advantage streams, multi-step return targets, a categorical distributional value representation, and noisy linear layers for exploration. The shared convolutional encoder feeds the dueling distributional head, and prioritized replay emphasizes transitions with large learning error. The methodology studies whether these individually useful components remain compatible when trained jointly in a single value-based system.

records.title: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model

MuZero learns three neural components: a representation function that maps observations to latent states, a dynamics function that predicts the next latent state and reward after an action, and a prediction function that outputs policy and value estimates. Monte Carlo Tree Search operates entirely in the learned latent space to select actions. Training targets are produced from observed rewards, search-improved policies, and bootstrapped values. The model therefore learns only the aspects of environment dynamics needed for planning, without reconstructing raw observations.

records.title: Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mastering Chess and Shogi by Self-Play with a General Reinforcement Learning Algorithm

AlphaZero uses a deep residual network that maps a board position to both a policy over legal moves and a scalar value estimate. Monte Carlo Tree Search uses these predictions to guide exploration and produces an improved search policy. Games are generated entirely by self-play using this search policy. The network is then updated to match the search visit distribution and final game outcome. Repeating self-play, search, and supervised-style policy/value updates allows the agent to learn without human game data or handcrafted evaluation functions.

records.title: Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Decision Transformer: Reinforcement Learning via Sequence Modeling

Decision Transformer reframes offline reinforcement learning as conditional autoregressive sequence modeling. Trajectories are represented as interleaved return-to-go, state, and action tokens with timestep embeddings and fed to a causal Transformer. During training, the model predicts actions conditioned on previous trajectory context and the desired remaining return. At inference, the user supplies a target return and current state, the model generates an action, and the return-to-go is updated as rewards are observed. No explicit Bellman backup or policy-gradient objective is required.

records.title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
records.methodology_paraphrase:
Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models

DreamerV3 learns a recurrent state-space world model from replayed experience. The encoder maps observations to compact representations, a stochastic latent dynamics model predicts future latent states and rewards, and a decoder reconstructs observations as an auxiliary learning signal. Actor and critic networks are optimized almost entirely from imagined trajectories rolled out inside the learned model. Robust normalization, categorical latent variables, and carefully balanced losses allow the same algorithm and hyperparameter recipe to operate across very different action spaces and observation domains.
